open_gaps: No learned allocator has been evaluated under realistic packet loss or delay. CV_MRTA_Benchmark (arXiv 2609.13711) tests Bernoulli, Gilbert-Elliott and Rayleigh loss on classical allocators only. MDGAM models communication range but explicitly not bandwidth, delay or loss. HeteroMRTA assumes 'global communication'. PARCO, Sadcher, ET and DPN are centralized.

Learned MRTA policies lose to trivial or exact baselines outside their training regime. Sadcher's own scaling study shows Greedy beating S-Sadcher for N=20 robots once M>70 tasks. HeteroMRTA is 15-23% worse than CTAS-D MILP wherever MILP finishes. Learned bidding in CBBA degrades with team size and needs 11-13 vs 6-9 consensus rounds.

On public min-max mTSP instances, learned solvers are not SOTA. On mTSPLib, ScheduleNet reaches 1.05-1.13x and DAN 1.11-1.18x vs LKH3 at 1.00x. GaS, DPN and ET all trail LKH3 at small m. The dedicated HGA (C&OR 2024) is rarely used as a baseline.

On public VRP libraries, neural solvers are not SOTA. The 2026 survey (arXiv 2602.21761) finds they 'generally underperform SOTA heuristics' on CVRPLIB X, and that 'heuristic baselines in most NRS literature lag behind SOTA'. The strongest 'beats HGS' claim (NDS) uses uniform synthetic instances only.

There is no community benchmark with a leaderboard for decentralized, dynamic, communication-limited task allocation. Most learned MRTA papers (CapAM, HeteroMRTA, Sadcher, MDGAM, MAGNNET, HIPPO-MAT) use their own generators, which reviewers will flag, exactly as they did for CBJA. The closest community benchmark is LoRR (grid scheduling plus planning, 2026 edition with delays and failures), and its 2026 instances are not yet in the public archive.

Multi-agent neural combinatorial optimization (PARCO, 2D-Ptr, CAMP, ECHO, GeoPAR) assumes perfect all-to-all attention during construction. None trains or tests with message dropout, stale information or partitioned communication graphs.

LLM-evolved heuristics (FunSearch, EoH, ReEvo, MCTS-AHD) have only been applied to single-agent or centralized combinatorial optimization. I found no verified work evolving decentralized bid, consensus or rebroadcast rules for CBBA/PI-style allocators, and none evaluated under packet loss.

Online and dynamic settings: the best verified dynamic-routing result (EURO-NeurIPS 2022 winner) is ML guiding an optimization layer, not an end-to-end policy. The MAPF lesson is similar: simple imitation learning plus a CS-PIBT shield beats large-scale imitation learning. End-to-end learned policies look weakest exactly where the researcher wants to work.

Simple structural fixes compete with learning. GACA (grouping tasks before auctioning, no learning) reports about 97% median optimality vs 81-84% for CBBA, which beats the learned-bidding variant from the same group. Any learned method must be compared against such strong non-learned variants, including DMCHBA, the lightest-messaging robust baseline under degraded communication.

sota_opportunities.idea: Evolve communication-robust decentralized allocation protocols with an LLM, i.e., ReEvo or MCTS-AHD style program search over the bid function, the consensus and rebroadcast policy, and the timeout/repair rules of a CBBA/PI/DMCHBA skeleton. The fitness is measured under a mix of Bernoulli, Gilbert-Elliott and Rayleigh loss. The output is interpretable code that needs no neural inference on the robot. Report results on held-out loss conditions, larger teams, and a dynamic-arrival extension.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: CV_MRTA_Benchmark (github.com/jlott22/CV_MRTA_Benchmark), all 25 conditions plus its scale studies up to 24 robots. Add a transfer test on HeteroMRTA's RALTestSet with lossy broadcast in place of global communication.
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: DMCHBA (MinMax 24.78 steps, 2.08 publications per step), DGA (24.49), HIPC (MinSum 66.95), ACBBA, PI, CBAA, plus GACA-style grouping and learned-bidding CBBA (2605.21932) if reimplemented
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: The benchmark is from Sep 2026, has no learned or evolved allocators, and LLM heuristic design has never targeted decentralized communication-limited allocation. It also builds on the researcher's CBBA and degraded-communication expertise from CBJA, and 4xH100 can serve an open LLM for the evolution loop.
sota_opportunities.risk: The benchmark is new and small (4-robot core, static tasks, grid), so reviewers may call it niche. It must be extended to dynamic tasks and larger teams, with a public release. Evolved code may overfit the simulator's loss model, which calls for held-out loss families. And if the win over DMCHBA is small, it becomes another 'what matters' paper.

sota_opportunities.idea: Enter the LoRR scheduling track with a hybrid scheduler: a GPU-batched learned task-scoring network (imitation from strong archived 2024 schedulers or a lookahead oracle) feeding a classical assignment solver (Hungarian or auction), plus a delay-robust re-assignment rule for the 2026 execution-uncertainty model. The design follows the NDS and EURO-NeurIPS pattern of a learned component guiding an optimization layer.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: LoRR Benchmark-Archive 2024 instances with archived best-known solutions (Scheduler and Combined tracks), and the 2026 delay/failure instances once archived
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: Archived 2024 Main Round entries: Scheduler track top score 6.876 (Team_No_Man's_Sky), Combined 9.842, together with each instance's best-known task counts. Planner fixed to the archived default or a top planner.
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: LoRR is the only community leaderboard covering allocation under 1 s per step with thousands of robots. Learned work so far (SILLM, MAPF-GPT) targets path planning, not scheduling. The 2026 edition adds communication and execution failures.
sota_opportunities.risk: Top entries are heavily engineered C++. Throughput gains may come from the planner, not the scheduler. The 2026 instances and results were not public in the archive when checked, and it is a grid abstraction rather than continuous robots.

sota_opportunities.idea: A communication-robust parallel multi-agent policy: take PARCO's parallel autoregressive design, but restrict each agent's attention to its current communication graph and stale message cache. Train with random message dropout and Gilbert-Elliott bursts, then add a lightweight CBBA-style consensus repair for conflicts. Show that (a) it matches PARCO at full communication and (b) it degrades gracefully while PARCO and 2D-Ptr collapse under loss.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: PARCO's released HCVRP and OMDCPDP test sets (N=60/100, M=3-20, plus N=1000, M=200 generalization) under full and degraded communication
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: PARCO sampling (HCVRP N100 M5: 6.36, +3.08% vs SISR 6.17), 2D-Ptr, DPN, ET, SISR, OR-Tools; under degraded communication also CBBA and DMCHBA
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: All multi-agent neural combinatorial optimization assumes lossless all-to-all attention during construction, and nobody has measured how it degrades.
sota_opportunities.risk: Under full communication it may not beat PARCO or SISR, so the SOTA claim would rest on the degraded-communication regime the researcher defines, the same weakness CBJA hit. Degrading a centralized solver may be seen as a strawman.

sota_opportunities.idea: Neural deconstruction search for min-max multi-agent routing: a learned destroy policy plus a split-DP / greedy-insertion repair (following NDS and the GaS optimal-split idea), aimed at beating HGA and LKH3 on public min-max mTSP instances under equal time budgets.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: mTSPLib (16 instances) plus the GaS/DPN/ET uniform sets (n=50-500, m=2-50) and TSPLIB-derived larger instances
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: HGA (Mahmoudinazlou & Kwon 2024, github.com/Sasanm88/m-TSP), LKH3 (600 s), RL-CMSA (2602.23579), GaS, DPN, ET
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: NDS beat HGS and PyVRP on single-fleet VRPs at equal time, but no min-max multi-agent version exists. Constructive learned min-max solvers all still trail LKH3 at small m.
sota_opportunities.risk: mTSPLib is tiny and already solved to near-optimal by LKH3 and CPLEX, so there is little headroom. The problem is centralized and static, drifting away from the decentralized group-mission framing.

sota_opportunities.idea: Imitation learning followed by RL fine-tuning, with a greedy-fallback safety layer, for heterogeneous coalition MRTA at large team sizes. This is Sadcher's own stated future work; add partial-observation training so it transfers to decentralized use.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: Sadcher 250K dataset plus its N=20, M up to 250 scaling protocol; HeteroMRTA RALTestSet
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: S-Sadcher (3.8% gap), Sadcher (6.8%), S-HeteroMRTA (10.8%), Greedy (20.4% small; best at N=20, M>70), CTAS-D MILP
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: Both learned methods lose to Greedy on large teams because demonstrations are missing there.
sota_opportunities.risk: Incremental over a single-lab MRS 2025 dataset with low benchmark credibility. Centralized unless extended.

sota_methods.name: GRAND (Guidance, Rebalancing, and Assignment for Networked Dispatch)
sota_methods.key_idea: Centralized hierarchical lifelong-MAPD scheduler. A GNN policy trained with RL outputs a desired regional distribution of free agents over an aggregated graph. Min-cost-flow rebalancing between regions follows, then decoupled local bipartite assignment. Runs within the 1 s/step budget.
sota_methods.problem: Lifelong multi-agent pickup-and-delivery task scheduling (LoRR Task Scheduling track setting)
sota_methods.code_url: none found (paper gives no code link)
sota_methods.benchmark_used: LoRR simulator with its own generated warehouse, room and maze maps (100-500 agents, 598-2537 tiles). Planner is Traffic-Flow-Guided PIBT. It does NOT use the official 10k-agent 2024 main-round instances.
sota_methods.reported_results: Throughput, 200 agents / 975 tiles, with reassignment: Greedy 16952, LoRR-2024 winner 18752, GRAND 20752, G-OPT (Hungarian) 19781. Without reassignment: 12372 / 12990 / 17916 / 16554. Room (200 agents): 10993 / 12561 / 14912 / 13801. Maze (400 agents): 1508 / 2013 / 2417 / 2062. Abstract claims up to +10% over the 2024 winning scheduler. Training takes about 24 h on one RTX 8000.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: No code. Homogeneous agents. No execution delays (the 2026 LoRR feature). Only up to 500 agents, on self-generated maps rather than the official competition instances. Deadlock and extreme-congestion regimes are explicitly excluded. Centralized.

sota_methods.name: LoRR 2024 Task-Scheduling-track winner (Team No Man's Sky)
sota_methods.key_idea: Heuristic that ranks agent-task pairs with a customized cost metric (as described by GRAND). Runs inside the LoRR start-kit with the default planner.
sota_methods.problem: Lifelong MAPD task scheduling, centralized, 1 s per step
sota_methods.venue: League of Robot Runners 2024 competition (Amazon Robotics sponsored). Code archived by the organizers.
sota_methods.license: Code-Archive has no LICENSE (GitHub API: null). Start-Kit is MIT.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Official LoRR 2024 main-round instances (10 instances: CITY-01/02, GAME, RANDOM-01..05, SORTATION, WAREHOUSE; up to 10,000 agents)
sota_methods.reported_results: Scheduler-track main-round score 6.876, 1st of 22 entries (2nd: Team_verstand 6.375). Tasks finished per instance: CITY-01 7324, CITY-02 14443, GAME 9130, RANDOM-01 571, RANDOM-02 938, RANDOM-03 1209, RANDOM-04 867, RANDOM-05 1380, SORTATION 146375, WAREHOUSE 146398. The same team won the Combined track with 9.842. All values parsed from the Code-Archive 2024 README.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: No peer-reviewed description. It is a hand-tuned heuristic. Team identity: GRAND cites Yukhnevich & Andreychuk 2025 for it (UNVERIFIED mapping).

sota_methods.name: Flow-Based Task Assignment for Large-Scale Online MAPD
sota_methods.key_idea: Casts online MAPD task assignment as a min-cost flow on the environment graph. This avoids pairwise distance computation. Congestion-aware edge costs and guide paths are passed to a Guided-PIBT planner.
sota_methods.problem: Online / lifelong MAPD task assignment at very large scale
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Random, warehouse-small and sortation-large maps, plus LoRR-style warehouse maps and game maps up to 6.5M cells. Uses its own C++ framework, not the LoRR start-kit.
sota_methods.reported_results: Sortation-large with 20,000 agents: 31,658 tasks (+15.91% over greedy). Warehouse-small with 600 agents: 6,185 tasks (+10.59%). Makespan 8-27% better than RMCA. Handles over 20k agents within 1 s.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Does not compare against LoRR competition winners or GRAND. Does not use the official instances or the start-kit. No code. Centralized.

sota_methods.name: PARCO (Parallel AutoRegressive Combinatorial Optimization)
sota_methods.key_idea: Neural solver trained with RL for multi-agent CO. Uses transformer communication layers between agents, a multiple-pointer head so all agents decode in parallel, and learned-priority conflict handlers.
sota_methods.problem: Multi-agent routing and scheduling: min-max HCVRP, OMDCPDP, FFSP
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Standard random HCVRP (N=60/100, M=3/5/7), OMDCPDP (N=50/100, M=5..20) and FFSP instances
sota_methods.reported_results: HCVRP gap to SISR: 8.37% (60,3), 10.00% (60,5), 11.68% (60,7), 6.71% (100,3), 7.13% (100,5), 7.64% (100,7), at about 0.04-0.06 s. Better than 2D-Ptr (8-14%), ET (14-23%) and DPN (12-19%). OMDCPDP: PARCO 3.84% (50,5) vs OR-Tools 4.61% and MAPDP 4.09%; 3.67% (100,10) vs OR-Tools 4.99%. Up to 24.7x faster than autoregressive baselines.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Still 6.7-11.7% behind the classical SISR heuristic on HCVRP. Construction is centralized with full information. No communication loss and no online arrivals.

sota_methods.name: SADCHER
sota_methods.key_idea: Imitation learning from 250K MILP-optimal schedules. A graph-attention and transformer model predicts robot-task assignment rewards, and a matching step turns them into assignments. Handles heterogeneous skills, dynamic coalitions and precedence constraints in real time. The S-variant samples several rollouts.
sota_methods.problem: Heterogeneous multi-robot scheduling with coalitions and precedence (ST-MR-TA with temporal constraints)
sota_methods.license: Code: no license (GitHub API null). Dataset: CC BY 4.0.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: MRTA-Benchmark 250K (8 tasks, 3 robots, 3 skills, optimal MILP) plus generalization up to 250 tasks and 20 robots
sota_methods.reported_results: Optimality gap in the 8t/3r training domain: S-Sadcher 3.8%, Sadcher 6.8% (22 ms per decision), S-HeteroMRTA 10.8%, Greedy 20.4%, HeteroMRTA 21.5%. At 20 robots performance degrades and Greedy is competitive beyond about 70 tasks.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Centralized. Optimal labels exist only for tiny instances. Degrades at 20 robots. Small venue. Code has no license.

sota_methods.name: HeteroMRTA (RL for heterogeneous MRTA and scheduling)
sota_methods.key_idea: Attention-based policy trained with REINFORCE (POMO-style baseline). Heterogeneous agents make sequential, decentralized-at-execution decisions to form and disband coalitions that minimize makespan.
sota_methods.problem: Heterogeneous ST-MR task allocation with coalition formation (makespan)
sota_methods.venue: IEEE RA-L vol. 10(3), pp. 2654-2661, 2025 (via ADS record)
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Self-generated SA-BT / SA-AT / MA-AT instance sets. Compared against CTAS-D (Gurobi MILP), SAS and TACO.
sota_methods.reported_results: Makespan optimality gap under 23% vs exact solutions even in the worst case, 100% success rate, at least two orders of magnitude faster than MILP. CTAS-D success drops to 0-40% on larger sets within 600-3600 s.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Beaten by SADCHER on the 250K benchmark (21.5% vs 3.8% gap). Uses self-generated instances. Assumes ideal communication.

sota_methods.name: ML-CO pipeline for dynamic VRPTW (Baty, Jungel, Klein, Parmentier, Schiffer)
sota_methods.key_idea: Structured learning with a combinatorial-optimization layer (prize-collecting HGS) decides which requests to dispatch each epoch. Trained against anticipative lower-bound targets.
sota_methods.problem: Dynamic fleet dispatch and routing with time windows (online arrivals)
sota_methods.venue: Transportation Science 58(4):708-725, 2024. Ranked first in the EURO Meets NeurIPS 2022 VRP competition (authors' claim).
sota_methods.benchmark_used: EURO Meets NeurIPS 2022 DVRPTW (ORTEC real-world instances, controller.py protocol)
sota_methods.reported_results: Final leaderboard (quickstart README): team 'Kleopatra' was overall rank 1 and dynamic rank 1 with dynamic cost 348,831.6, vs Team_sb 358,161.4 and OptiML 359,270.1. That Kleopatra is the Baty et al. team is inferred from the 'ranked first' claim and is UNVERIFIED.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Single-depot centralized dispatcher, not a robot team. The final hidden-phase instances are not public, so exact leaderboard reproduction is imperfect.

sota_methods.name: LaMMA-P (LM-driven multi-agent PDDL planner)
sota_methods.key_idea: An LLM decomposes a natural-language instruction and allocates subtasks to heterogeneous robots by skill. It then generates PDDL problems, which Fast Downward solves. Results are validated in AI2-THOR.
sota_methods.problem: Language-conditioned long-horizon heterogeneous multi-robot task allocation and planning
sota_methods.benchmark_used: MAT-THOR: 70 tasks (30 compound, 20 complex, 20 vague), AI2-THOR
sota_methods.reported_results: GPT-4o success rate: compound 0.93, complex 0.77, vague 0.45, vs SMART-LLM (GPT-4o) 0.70 / 0.20 / 0.00. With Llama-3.1-8B: 0.45 / 0.15 / 0.00. Claims +105% success rate and +36% efficiency over prior LM planners.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Tiny benchmark (70 tasks), so high variance. Depends on GPT-4o. Small open models collapse. Centralized. No communication or degradation model.

sota_methods.name: DGA / HIPC / DMCHBA (classical decentralized leaders on the CV MRTA benchmark)
sota_methods.key_idea: DGA: evolutionary team-plan search. HIPC: implicit local-team greedy planning plus plan consensus (Hybrid Information and Plan Consensus). DMCHBA: low-traffic market/consensus hybrid. All are compared against CBAA, ACBBA and PI in one shared event-driven robot shell.
sota_methods.problem: Decentralized multi-robot task allocation under degraded communication (Collaborative Visit)
sota_methods.venue: Benchmark paper is an arXiv preprint (Sept 2026)
sota_methods.license: None: the README says no reuse license is granted
sota_methods.benchmark_used: CV MRTA Benchmark: 4 robots, 10 targets, 19x19 grid, 500 paired instances, 25 conditions (Bernoulli, Gilbert-Elliott, Rayleigh)
sota_methods.reported_results: Mean MinMax over the 24 impaired conditions: DGA 24.49, DMCHBA 24.78, HIPC 25.12 steps. MinSum: HIPC 66.95, DGA 67.22 (top two in every impaired condition). DMCHBA has the lowest traffic at 2.08 publications per team step. Median compute ranges from 4.88 ms (DMCHBA) to 1.346 s (DGA).
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: No optimality gaps reported. Tiny scale. No dynamic task arrivals. Payload bandwidth not measured (authors' own limitations). Leaders differ by only about 1%.

sota_methods.name: ED-CBBA (Event-Driven CBBA)
sota_methods.key_idea: Event-triggered message transmission for CBBA that keeps CBBA's convergence and performance bounds.
sota_methods.problem: Decentralized MRTA with limited bandwidth
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Self-built Monte-Carlo simulations
sota_methods.reported_results: Up to 52% fewer message transmissions with CBBA-equivalent allocation performance
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Self-built testbed. Not evaluated on the CV benchmark or any public benchmark.

sota_methods.name: Event-Triggered Adaptive Consensus for MRTA
sota_methods.key_idea: Negotiation is triggered only by events, consensus intensity adapts to demand, and behavior trees handle execution resilience in heterogeneous swarms.
sota_methods.problem: Communication-efficient decentralized MRTA with failures
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Own simulation. Baselines: reactive, information sharing, CBBA, periodic CBBA+BT, C-CBBA.
sota_methods.reported_results: Significantly lower network overhead with top mission effectiveness (qualitative in abstract; exact numbers not extracted)
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Self-built testbed. No public numbers to beat.

sota_methods.name: CC-OPI
sota_methods.key_idea: Online distributed task allocation for UAV swarms that interleaves negotiation with execution. Uses topology-adaptive cost metrics and version-based fault tolerance, and replans only on physical or topological events.

benchmarks.name: League of Robot Runners (LoRR): Start-Kit, Benchmark-Archive and Code-Archive; 2023, 2024 and 2026 editions
benchmarks.problem_class: Lifelong MAPD / lifelong MAPF on grids with rotation actions. Separate Task Scheduling, Planning/Execution and Combined tracks. The 2026 edition adds execution delays (bernoulli or poisson delay events, uniform or gaussian durations, hidden parameters). Centralized, 1 s per step, up to 10,000 agents.
benchmarks.license: Start-Kit: MIT (38 stars, pushed 2026-07-15, version 3.1.0). Benchmark-Archive and Code-Archive: no LICENSE file, so ask the organizers before redistributing.
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Yes. Best-known solutions are published per instance for 2023 and 2024. The full 2024 main-round leaderboard, including the Scheduler track (22 entries, winner No Man's Sky 6.876), is in the Code-Archive README with the code for every leaderboard entry. The 2026 main round ran Apr 14 - Jul 23, 2026 (site API), with results announced Aug 7, 2026 (CFP). The 2026 results and instances are NOT yet in the Benchmark-Archive: a clone on 2026-09-27 contains only 2023 and 2024. 2026 winners are UNVERIFIED.
benchmarks.baselines_included: Default greedy scheduler, default Traffic-Flow-Guided PIBT planner, default TPG executor, and all archived team entries. Published papers to compare against: GRAND (2512.03194) and Flow-based TA (2508.05890).
benchmarks.metrics: Total tasks finished (throughput) per instance. Leaderboard score is the sum across instances of each entry's normalized ratio to the best known. Time-to-task and time-in-task are also reported by GRAND.
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: Medium. C++ with pybind11 Python interface (--schedulerPython). Scheduler track: implement TaskScheduler::plan(time_limit, proposed_schedule) with the default planner and executor held fixed. Needs a CPU farm for 10k-agent instances (96 cores suffices). A decentralized allocator has to be emulated inside a centralized call.
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: HIGH for AAMAS, ICAPS, IJCAI and ICRA. It is Amazon-sponsored, co-hosted with AAMAS 2026, has archived instances, best-known solutions and winner code. 'Beats the LoRR 2024 scheduling winner on the official main-round instances under the start-kit time limits' is a claim reviewers accept. Caveat: centralized, so it does not test degraded communication.

benchmarks.name: CV MRTA Benchmark (Collaborative Visit, degraded communication)
benchmarks.problem_class: Decentralized MRTA (visit targets; MinMax and MinSum travel) under Bernoulli, Gilbert-Elliott and Rayleigh-fading loss, in both asynchronous execution and pre-allocation modes. 4 robots, 10 targets, 19x19 grid. Scale studies vary the grid from 14 to 34 and targets from 5 to 50.
benchmarks.license: No license. The README states public availability grants no right to adapt or redistribute. Paper uses the arXiv non-exclusive license.
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Published numbers, no leaderboard. About 75,000-row results CSVs cover 112,500 core simulations. Impaired-condition means: MinMax DGA 24.49 / DMCHBA 24.78 / HIPC 25.12; MinSum HIPC 66.95 / DGA 67.22; traffic 2.08 publications per team step (DMCHBA).
benchmarks.baselines_included: CBAA, ACBBA, PI, HIPC, DMCHBA, DGA, with frozen objective-specific configurations. The companion paper 2609.06273 covers bundle-length tuning under loss. Predecessor comparison studies are both in RA-L: Nayak et al. 2020 (CBAA, ACBBA, DHBA, HIPC, PI) and Cao et al. (CBAA, CBBA, DHBA, HIPC, PI, DGA; year given as 2025 by the CV paper but 2023 by the IEEE record; UNVERIFIED).
benchmarks.metrics: MinMax and MinSum travel (steps), publication intensity (messages per team step), allocation reliability and viability, full-protocol compute time, scale sensitivity
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: High technically: Python, a shared allocator interface, a Manhattan cost model, and a size close to CBJA's CBBA code. Low legally: you need the authors' permission or a clean-room reimplementation of the protocol.
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: LOW-MODERATE. It is the most on-topic benchmark for this line of work (decentralized allocation under degraded communication with published external baselines), but it is 2 weeks old, a preprint, 0 stars, tiny scale, and the leaders differ by about 1%. It is better than a self-built testbed but will not read as an established SOTA venue. Pair it with a scaled-up and dynamic-arrival extension, and report optimality gaps.

open_gaps: No established, licensed, leaderboard-backed benchmark exists for decentralized MRTA under degraded communication. The only one with published multi-baseline numbers (CV MRTA, arXiv 2609.13711) is 2 weeks old, has no reuse license, and covers 4 robots and 10 targets. Its two RA-L predecessors (Nayak et al. 2020; Cao et al.) are comparison studies with no public code located.

The CV MRTA benchmark reports achieved travel, not optimality gaps, and omits dynamic task arrivals and payload bandwidth (authors' own limitations). Headroom above DGA (MinMax 24.49) and HIPC (MinSum 66.95) is unknown and may be about 1%, the spread between the leaders.
LoRR is centralized with a 1 s/step budget. No scheduling track models communication loss or decentralized allocation, and the 2026 execution-delay model has hidden parameters.

GRAND, the only arXiv scheduler paper claiming to beat the LoRR 2024 winner, uses self-generated maps of at most 500 agents. It has no code and no delays, and was never tested on the official 10k-agent main-round instances. Flow-based TA (2508.05890) never compares against LoRR winners.

An arXiv search for 'Robot Runners' (2026-09-27) found no published delay-aware or robust task-scheduling paper for the LoRR 2026 execution-uncertainty setting. The 2026 instances and best-known solutions are not yet in the Benchmark-Archive (only 2023 and 2024 are present). The search was title/abstract only, so this is UNVERIFIED beyond that.
Learned multi-agent CO solvers remain 6.7-11.7% behind the classical SISR heuristic on min-max HCVRP (PARCO, NeurIPS 2025) and ignore communication and online arrivals.

Learned heterogeneous MRTA methods (HeteroMRTA, SADCHER) train on tiny optimal instances (8 tasks x 3 robots). SADCHER degrades at 20 robots, where Greedy becomes competitive beyond about 70 tasks. All are centralized with ideal communication.

Language-conditioned multi-robot benchmarks are tiny (MAT-THOR 70 tasks, COHERENT 100) and dominated by GPT-4o pipelines. Small on-board models (Llama-3.1-8B in LaMMA-P) collapse, for example 0.00 success on vague commands. No benchmark combines language-gated permissions with degraded communication.

Recent decentralized communication-aware allocators (ED-CBBA, Event-Triggered Adaptive Consensus, CC-OPI, IBR) all use self-built testbeds with no shared protocol, so claims cannot be compared. This is the same weakness that sank CBJA.

Not verified because the web-search budget was exhausted: SMAC task-allocation relevance, LoRR 2026 winners and scores, whether team Kleopatra is Baty et al., whether No Man's Sky is Yukhnevich & Andreychuk, the year of Cao et al. RA-L, and code availability for CoCoBench, MultiUAV-Plat and CC-OPI.

sota_opportunities.idea: Delay-robust, congestion-aware lifelong scheduler for LoRR. A learned global guidance model (GNN on the H100s) supplies regional agent-demand targets, and a CBBA-style local market handles assignment with incremental deadline and commitment rules. This reuses CBJA's finding that a simple incremental deadline rule matches VOC. The scheduler hedges against delays (bernoulli/poisson) by reserving slack and reassigning tasks whose first errand has not started. Evaluate as a pure Scheduler-track entry: default planner and executor fixed, official time limits.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: LoRR 2024 official main-round instances (10 instances, up to 10k agents) through the Start-Kit v3.1.0 scheduler interface, plus the 2026 delay settings once the archive is released (until then, use start-kit delay generators with disclosed parameters)
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: GRAND beat the 2024 winner only on its own maps of at most 500 agents, with no delays and no code. Flow-based TA never compared against winners. No published scheduler targets the 2026 execution-uncertainty setting. The LoRR scheduler track has public best-known numbers per instance and archived winner code, so the comparison is externally anchored rather than self-built.
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: LoRR 2024 Scheduler winner No Man's Sky: score 6.876, e.g. WAREHOUSE 146,398 and SORTATION 146,375 tasks, CITY-02 14,443. Runner-up Team_verstand 6.375. Default greedy. G-OPT/Hungarian. GRAND reimplemented (reported +10.7% over the winner at 200 agents: 20,752 vs 18,752). Flow-based TA reimplemented.
sota_opportunities.risk: HIGH engineering load: C++ performance at 10k agents within 1 s/step. The 2026 delay parameters are hidden and 2026 instances are unarchived. Centralized evaluation moves away from the decentralized/degraded-communication identity. The Code-Archive has no license, so comparisons must be run on unmodified winner code. Gains on huge instances may be dominated by the planner rather than the scheduler.

sota_opportunities.idea: A decentralized allocator that Pareto-dominates DGA, HIPC and DMCHBA across all 24 impaired communication conditions: MinMax at or below DGA, MinSum at or below HIPC, traffic near DMCHBA's 2.08 publications per team step, compute in milliseconds. Candidate design: HIPC-style implicit local-team planning plus loss-adaptive bundle length (motivated by 2609.06273) plus learned peer-behavior prediction. First, measure headroom with an exact MILP (4 robots x 10 targets is trivial) and publish optimality gaps. Then extend to 16-50 robots and dynamic arrivals to address the benchmark's stated limitations.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: CV MRTA Benchmark (arXiv 2609.13711), reusing its 500 paired instances and 25 conditions. Reproduce the Nayak et al. 2020 and Cao et al. RA-L protocols for lineage.
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: The benchmark appeared on 2026-09-12. It reports no optimality gaps, no learned or hybrid allocators and no dynamic arrivals. The leaders trade off objectives (DGA vs HIPC vs DMCHBA), so none is Pareto-best. This is exactly the researcher's niche (CBBA-derived, degraded communication).
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: Impaired means: DGA MinMax 24.49, DMCHBA 24.78, HIPC 25.12. MinSum: HIPC 66.95, DGA 67.22. Also CBAA, ACBBA and PI under the same shell.
sota_opportunities.risk: The repo has no license, so you need written permission or a clean-room protocol reimplementation. Headroom may be about 1-3% and not statistically separable, which is the CBJA failure mode again. Reviewers may see a 2-week-old unlicensed preprint benchmark as barely better than self-built. Mitigate by first computing MILP optimality gaps: if the leaders are already within 2% of optimal, abandon this route.

sota_opportunities.idea: Close the neural-vs-classical gap on multi-agent routing. PARCO-style parallel decoding plus GPU-batched learned local search or decentralized agent-wise repair, trained on 4x H100, targeting a gap below 3% to SISR on min-max HCVRP at under 1 s, while keeping OMDCPDP leadership.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: PARCO/RL4CO suites: HCVRP N=60/100 with M=3/5/7; OMDCPDP; FFSP
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: The best learned solver (PARCO, NeurIPS 2025) still trails SISR by 6.7-11.7% on HCVRP. The MIT code and standard generators make the comparison clean and reproducible.
sota_opportunities.risk: A crowded field with strong groups (ai4co, KAIST). Weak link to decentralized robot missions and communication degradation, so novelty would have to come from the learning side. Classical SISR/HGS with longer budgets may still win.

sota_opportunities.idea: Heterogeneous coalition scheduling with precedence that beats S-SADCHER. For example, SADCHER-style imitation plus RL fine-tuning and test-time search on GPU. Target: below 3.8% gap in the 8t/3r domain and a clear win over Greedy at 20 robots and more than 70 tasks, where SADCHER degrades. Optionally add a decentralized execution variant under packet loss.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: MRTA-Benchmark 250K (CC BY 4.0), using SADCHER's generalization protocol (up to 250 tasks, 3/5/20 robots)
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: Only one paper (MRS 2025) evaluates on the dataset. It reports explicit failure at 20 robots, and all methods are centralized with ideal communication.
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: S-Sadcher 3.8%, Sadcher 6.8%, S-HeteroMRTA 10.8%, Greedy 20.4%, HeteroMRTA 21.5% optimality gaps. MILP optimal for 8x3.
sota_opportunities.risk: The venue tier of prior work is modest, so a win may not read as SOTA to top venues. Optimal labels exist only at tiny scale, so large-scale claims lack a ground-truth reference. SADCHER code has no license.

sota_opportunities.idea: Reuse CBJA's System-1 assets for language-gated allocation. A small on-board model (Kev/Jev-style or an 8B model) parses skills and permissions, and an exact or classical allocator plus PDDL planner does the rest. The aim is to match GPT-4o LaMMA-P success at a fraction of the cost and to fix small-model collapse on vague commands.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: MAT-THOR (LaMMA-P); secondarily COHERENT's 100-task benchmark or CoCoBench
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: LaMMA-P with Llama-3.1-8B scores 0.45 / 0.15 / 0.00 success (compound / complex / vague) vs 0.93 / 0.77 / 0.45 with GPT-4o. No work shows small models closing this gap.
sota_opportunities.risk: Only 70 tasks, so statistical power is weak. Reviewers discount LLM-benchmark SOTA. There are no degraded-communication or decentralization aspects, and it is off the MRTA-optimization core.

sweeps.area: LLM / foundation-model multi-robot and multi-agent embodied planning and task allocation (2023-2026), and the decentralized consensus-auction MRTA line relevant to a System-1 + consensus hybrid (successor to CBJA)

sota_methods.name: PARTNR baselines: ReAct (Llama-3.1-70B) centralized/decentralized, plus a fine-tuned Llama-3.1-8B planner
sota_methods.problem: Two-agent (human/robot) household rearrangement from natural language with spatial, temporal and heterogeneous-capability constraints, in Habitat 3.0
sota_methods.benchmark_used: PARTNR (100k train / 1k val / 1k test episodes, 60 houses)
sota_methods.key_idea: The benchmark's own LLM planners: ReAct high-level planning over oracle or learned skills. It compares single, centralized and decentralized control and full vs partial observability. A small model fine-tuned on the planning data is also included.
sota_methods.reported_results: Table 2 (SR / sim steps): ReAct decentralized, oracle skills, partial obs 0.73 / 3295 steps / 15.24 planning cycles. Centralized, partial 0.74 / 2298. Centralized, full 0.74 / 1347. Heuristic-Expert (privileged, full obs) 0.84 / 1261. Finetuned 8B decentralized 0.70 / 3229 / 12.85 cycles, 8.6x faster inference than 70B. With learned skills 0.57; with learned skills + ConceptGraph perception 0.30. Humans: 0.93. With a real human, the LLM needs 1.5x the steps of two humans.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: The paper says SoTA LLMs show 'poor coordination and failures in task tracking and recovery'. Decentralized control needs about 2.4x the sim steps of the privileged heuristic. No leaderboard or eval server. Communication is perfect and implicit. Only 2 agents.

sota_methods.name: LLawCo (Learning Laws of Cooperation)
sota_methods.problem: Communicative embodied multi-agent cooperation
sota_methods.benchmark_used: PARTNR-Dialog (new: PARTNR plus explicit message passing; 2k train / 1k val) and TDW-MAT
sota_methods.key_idea: Agents distil 'laws of cooperation' from their own failure analyses and fine-tune them into the LLM. No stronger-model supervision is needed.
sota_methods.reported_results: PARTNR-Dialog SR: Qwen-3-14B 74% vs 70% (CommPARTNR). Llama-3.1-70B 75% vs 73% (ReAct). Average gain +4.5 pts on PARTNR-Dialog and +6.8 pts on TDW-MAT across 4 backbones.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Gains are small (2-4 pts). Dialogue channel is lossless. No latency or token-cost reporting found. Allocation is still implicit in LLM reasoning.

sota_methods.name: FLEET (Formal Language-Grounded Scheduling for Heterogeneous Robot Teams)
sota_methods.problem: Heterogeneous multi-robot scheduling from language
sota_methods.benchmark_used: PARTNR, a 2-agent subset split into constraint-free / heterogeneous / temporal (episode count not stated in the fetched text); hardware quadrupeds
sota_methods.key_idea: An LLM front end outputs a task graph with durations and precedence plus a robot-task capability fitness matrix. A MILP back end (CBC, 120 s cap, 1% gap) minimizes makespan. This is the closest published analogue to 'LLM parses, optimizer allocates'.
sota_methods.reported_results: Average SR 0.59 vs 0.28 for the PARTNR decentralized baseline and 0.57 for SMART-LLM centralized. By category: constraint-free 0.56, heterogeneous 0.67, temporal 0.53. Tested with GPT-4o and gpt-oss-20b.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Centralized MILP, and no communication model. Its PARTNR-decentralized baseline (0.28) differs sharply from the PARTNR paper's 0.73, so the setting is not comparable to the original table. No code.

sota_methods.name: CoTS (Collaborative Tree Search)
sota_methods.problem: Decentralized 2-agent embodied cooperation with natural-language communication
sota_methods.benchmark_used: TDW-MAT (24 test episodes) and C-WAH (10 tasks)
sota_methods.key_idea: Agents discuss long-term joint plans inside a shared, modified MCTS whose rewards come from LLM evaluation. A plan-evaluation module decides when to replan.
sota_methods.reported_results: TDW-MAT transport rate, GPT-4: 83 without oracle perception (CaPo 74, RoCo 72, CoELA 71) and 93 with oracle perception (CaPo 89, CoELA 85). C-WAH average steps, GPT-4: visual 81 / symbolic 49 (CaPo 83/51, CoELA 92/57). Cost per plan update: 7,923 characters and 26.8 s. With GPT-3.5, CaPo beats CoTS on some metrics.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Tiny test sets (24 and 10 episodes). GPT-4 is required for the gains. About 27 s of deliberation per plan update. The non-LLM heuristic pair CoRHP reaches 61 (no oracle) / 75 (oracle), above every GPT-3.5 LLM agent without oracle (52-59).

sota_methods.name: CaPo (Cooperative Plan Optimization)
sota_methods.problem: LLM embodied multi-agent cooperation efficiency
sota_methods.benchmark_used: TDW-MAT, C-WAH
sota_methods.key_idea: Agents write a meta-plan together through multi-turn discussion, then refine it adaptively as progress changes. At most 3 discussion rounds per planning cycle.
sota_methods.reported_results: TDW-MAT transport rate, GPT-4: 74 without oracle, 89 with oracle (CoELA 71/85). GPT-3.5: 57/84. C-WAH steps, GPT-4: symbolic 51, visual 83. Plan updates: 14-17 per task, 2.4 discussion rounds and about 1,757 characters each.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: The GitHub repo only says 'Code is coming soon!', so results cannot be reproduced from released code. CoTS surpasses it with GPT-4.

sota_methods.name: CoELA (Cooperative Embodied Language Agent)
sota_methods.problem: Decentralized embodied cooperation with costly communication
sota_methods.benchmark_used: TDW-MAT (24 test episodes), C-WAH
sota_methods.key_idea: Modular agent (perception, memory, communication, planning, execution) with LLM-generated messages.
sota_methods.reported_results: TDW-MAT transport rate, GPT-4: 71 without oracle, 85 with oracle. C-WAH steps: 92 visual, 57 symbolic (values as reproduced in the CoTS table).
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Greedy single-step planning. Messages are free text. It is the standard baseline that all later work beats.

sota_methods.name: CoBel-World (Collaborative Belief World)
sota_methods.venue: arXiv preprint (2509.21981v3, Jan 2026); an OpenReview PDF exists but acceptance was not verified
sota_methods.problem: Communication-efficient LLM multi-agent collaboration
sota_methods.benchmark_used: TDW-MAT, C-WAH (backbones Qwen3-32B, DeepSeek-V3.2, GPT-4o)
sota_methods.key_idea: Symbolic belief representation of the world and of teammates' intents, updated by zero-shot Bayesian-style LLM reasoning. Agents communicate only when a miscoordination is predicted.
sota_methods.reported_results: 64-79% less communication than the strongest baselines (CoELA, CaPo), 4-28% better completion efficiency, and about +4% transport rate on TDW-MAT (abstract / summary level).
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Not compared with CoTS in the fetched summary. Communication is lossless. Per-table numbers were not extracted.

sota_methods.name: ELHPlan (Action Chains)
sota_methods.problem: Token-efficient long-horizon multi-agent planning
sota_methods.benchmark_used: TDW-MAT, C-WAH
sota_methods.key_idea: Action sequences bound to sub-goal intentions, with proactive conflict checks and targeted refinement, instead of an LLM call every step.
sota_methods.reported_results: Comparable task success with only 30-40% of the tokens of SoTA methods. The authors argue token and planning-time metrics should be standard.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Claims efficiency, not higher success. Exact per-benchmark numbers not extracted.

sota_methods.name: Hierarchical LLM multi-agent framework with prompt optimization (Kawabe & Takano, NEC)
sota_methods.problem: Multi-robot task planning from language with PDDL back end
sota_methods.benchmark_used: MAT-THOR (70 tasks = 30 compound / 20 complex / 20 vague, 5 floor plans, 5 random inits per task)
sota_methods.key_idea: Layered LLM agents: upper layers decompose the instruction, lower layers write PDDL for Fast Downward (LAMA). After failures, textual-gradient prompt optimization updates meta-prompts shared across agents.
sota_methods.reported_results: GPT-4o SR: compound 0.95, complex 0.84, vague 0.60, vs LaMMA-P 0.93 / 0.77 / 0.45. Robot utilization 1.00 in all categories.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Centralized, perfect communication, static tasks. Does not say whether LaMMA-P numbers were re-run. No code.

sota_methods.name: LaMMA-P (LM-driven PDDL multi-agent planner)
sota_methods.problem: Heterogeneous multi-robot long-horizon task allocation and planning
sota_methods.benchmark_used: MAT-THOR (introduced here; AI2-THOR)
sota_methods.key_idea: An LLM does task decomposition and allocation. The LLM writes PDDL, Fast Downward solves it, and the resulting plans are merged.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Allocation is prompted, not optimized. Vague commands are weak. Other papers report much lower LaMMA-P numbers in their own settings (KGLAMP; EmboTeam on MACE-THOR: 12% SR).

sota_methods.name: KGLAMP (Knowledge-Graph-guided LM Adaptive Multi-robot Planning)
sota_methods.problem: Multi-robot planning and replanning after execution failures
sota_methods.benchmark_used: MAT-THOR (its own basic / complex / vague split and TCR metric)
sota_methods.key_idea: A knowledge graph of object relations, reachability and robot capabilities guides LLM-to-PDDL generation, with replanning on symbolic failures (triggered in about 24.5% of tasks).
sota_methods.reported_results: GPT-5 task completion rate: basic 84.0%, complex 68.4%, vague 71.4%. At least +25.3% over LaMMA-P, the strongest re-run baseline. Planning time 181.7-301.5 s per task. Small local models also tested (Llama-3.2-3B, Phi-3-mini, Mistral-7B, Qwen2-7B).
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Different metric and split from LaMMA-P and NEC, so the numbers cannot be compared directly. Planning takes minutes. No code.

sota_methods.name: LLaMAR (plan-act-correct-verify)
sota_methods.problem: Long-horizon multi-agent planning under partial observability
sota_methods.benchmark_used: MAP-THOR (45 tasks x 5 floor plans, 4 ambiguity levels; 2 agents in main runs) and a Search & Rescue environment
sota_methods.key_idea: Four LM modules (Planner, Actor, Corrector, Verifier) self-correct from execution feedback without an oracle. A centralized LLaMAR sees all agents' states.
sota_methods.reported_results: GPT-4V: SR 0.66, transport rate 0.91, coverage 0.97, balance 0.82, vs ReAct 0.34, Act 0.33, CoELA 0.25, SmartLLM 0.11. With 3 agents SR 0.70, with 5 agents 0.62. SAR: SR 0.44.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Centralized. 4 LM queries per decision step, and the authors admit higher cost and compute time. GPT-4V is discontinued (the README warns results may differ), so baselines must be re-run. No later paper beating it on MAP-THOR was found.

sota_methods.name: COHERENT (PEFA loop for heterogeneous robots)
sota_methods.problem: Heterogeneous team (quadrotor, dog, arm) task assignment
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Own 100-task BEHAVIOR-1K/OmniGibson benchmark (40 tasks evaluated)
sota_methods.key_idea: A centralized assigner proposes subtasks, robots execute them and send self-reflection feedback, and the assigner adjusts (Proposal-Execution-Feedback-Adjustment).
sota_methods.reported_results: gpt-4-0125-preview: SR 0.975 / 12.4 steps, vs CMRS 0.625, DMRS-1D 0.600, LLM-MCTS 0.200.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Near-saturated. Only 40 tasks evaluated. Isaac Sim 2022.2 dependency makes it hard to adopt. Centralized.

sota_methods.name: HMAS-2 (Scalable multi-robot collaboration, centralized vs decentralized)
sota_methods.problem: How LLM communication architecture affects success and token cost as the team grows
sota_methods.benchmark_used: BoxNet1, BoxNet2, Warehouse, BoxLift (2D; plus 3D variants)
sota_methods.key_idea: A central LLM planner, with each robot's local LLM giving feedback on the plan.
sota_methods.reported_results: GPT-4 SR: HMAS-2 82.5 / 57.5 / 62.5 / 100; CMAS 75 / 27.5 / 15 / 90; DMAS 25 / 0 / 0 / 52.5 (BoxNet1 / BoxNet2 / Warehouse / BoxLift). CMAS is the most token-efficient and scales worst in success.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: 2023-era GPT-4 numbers; the code is tied to the OpenAI API. Fully decentralized LLM dialogue does poorly.

sota_methods.name: EMOS (Robot Resume)
sota_methods.problem: Embodiment-aware heterogeneous multi-robot task allocation
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Habitat-MAS (ablations on 519 episodes; 70+ scenes)
sota_methods.key_idea: LLM agents build a 'robot resume' of their own capabilities from URDF and kinematics tools, then discuss allocation.
sota_methods.reported_results: GPT-4o: SR 37.82%, sub-goal SR 81.26%, 80,783 tokens and 2,358 sim steps per episode. Without the robot resume SR is 15.63%.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Low absolute SR. About 80k tokens per episode. The main table only compares ablations.

sota_methods.name: EmboTeam
sota_methods.problem: Multi-robot household collaboration: LLM to PDDL to behavior trees
sota_methods.benchmark_used: MACE-THOR (42 tasks, 8 layouts; parallel-independent and temporal-dependent splits)
sota_methods.key_idea: LLM parses the instruction to PDDL, a classical planner optimizes it, and the plan is compiled to reactive behavior trees that coordinate through a shared blackboard.
sota_methods.reported_results: Abstract: SR 12% to 55% and GCR 32% to 72% vs LaMMA-P. A third-party leaderboard page lists GPT-4o SR 71% (parallel) / 38% (temporal) vs LaMMA-P 14% / 10%.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Self-introduced benchmark; the two SR sources disagree (different aggregations). Centralized.

sota_methods.name: LDT-Coord (Communication-efficient digital-twin coordination)
sota_methods.problem: Communication-constrained coordination of heterogeneous LLM embodied agents
sota_methods.benchmark_used: RoCo/MuJoCo: 3 multi-arm coordination classes (mutual exclusion, synchronization, dependency)
sota_methods.key_idea: Agents send structured action and timing reports to a digital-twin server; a rule-based orchestrator resolves conflicts. Reporting is tuned as a constrained POMDP with PPO-Lagrangian. Includes path-loss uplink rate and per-step latency constraints.
sota_methods.reported_results: Homogeneous 1.5B agents: SR 0.640 with 43.3 bytes per episode. 73-90x less communication than dialogue methods (RoCo-NL, AutoGen) and 1.9-2.6x less than centralized baselines, at comparable success.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Small custom task set, not an established leaderboard. Central server. No code.

sota_methods.name: OSDAG (Online Scheduling over DAG)
sota_methods.problem: Latency and makespan in LLM multi-robot collaboration
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Custom PyBullet (5 tasks)
sota_methods.key_idea: The LLM parses the instruction once into a dependency and capability DAG. A lightweight online scheduler then dispatches ready tasks to idle robots.
sota_methods.reported_results: Reasoning 5-15x faster than RoCo. Makespan up to 38% lower (Task 5: 26.0 s vs 41.6 s). SR 80-100%, but only 80% vs 90% for ChatGPT-Prompts on Task 3.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Custom, tiny benchmark with 2-3 robots. Centralized scheduler.

sota_methods.name: GACA (Grouping Auction-Consensus Algorithm)
sota_methods.problem: Decentralized MRTA (classical, no language)
sota_methods.benchmark_used: 3,280 random instances, 5-20 agents, 10-50 tasks
sota_methods.key_idea: Robots bid on spatially coherent task clusters instead of single tasks inside an auction-consensus loop.
sota_methods.reported_results: Median percent optimality about 97% vs 81-84% for CBBA, converging in equal or fewer iterations.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: No communication degradation, no language, no public code. Same group also has a CBBA with RL-learned bids (arXiv 2605.21932, Ubiquitous Robots 2026).

sota_methods.name: HIPC / DMCHBA / DGA (best of the CV_MRTA degraded-communication benchmark)
sota_methods.license: README: no reuse license selected yet
sota_methods.problem: Decentralized MRTA under Bernoulli, Gilbert-Elliott and Rayleigh link degradation
sota_methods.benchmark_used: CV_MRTA_Benchmark (19x19 grid, 4 robots, 10 targets nominal; 25 communication conditions; 112,500 simulations)
sota_methods.key_idea: Head-to-head benchmark of CBAA, ACBBA, PI, HIPC, DMCHBA and DGA.
sota_methods.reported_results: MinMax: DGA 24.49, DMCHBA 24.78. MinSum: HIPC 66.95, DGA 67.22. HIPC and DMCHBA stay viable and stable in every condition; ACBBA, PI and DGA lose stability as links degrade. Compute ranges from 4.88 ms (DMCHBA) to 1.346 s (DGA). Companion paper 2609.06273: under 25% loss the best bundle length for ACBBA and PI shifts from 12 to 2.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: No language or semantic constraints. Very new (Sept 2026). The unlicensed code limits reuse.

sota_methods.name: SMART-LLM
sota_methods.problem: Few-shot LLM task decomposition, coalition formation and allocation
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Own AI2-THOR dataset; later used as a baseline in MAT-THOR, MAP-THOR and PARTNR
sota_methods.key_idea: Programmatic few-shot prompts carry the instruction through decomposition, coalition formation and task allocation.
sota_methods.reported_results: As a baseline: MAT-THOR (GPT-4o) SR 0.70 / 0.20 / 0.00. MAP-THOR SR 0.11. PARTNR subset (in FLEET) SR 0.57.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Open-loop; weak on complex and vague tasks.

sota_methods.name: AutoHMA-LLM
sota_methods.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking (IEEE Xplore doc 10839354)
sota_methods.problem: Cloud-edge hybrid LLM coordination for heterogeneous agents (logistics, inspection, search and rescue)
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Custom scenarios
sota_methods.key_idea: A cloud LLM plans centrally; device-side LLMs and generative agents do local feasibility checks.
sota_methods.reported_results: UNVERIFIED (search-snippet level only; the paper was not read): about 46% fewer communication steps, 31% fewer tokens, +5.7% task accuracy.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Custom benchmark, not comparable. Numbers not verified from the paper.

sota_methods.name: DART-LLM
sota_methods.problem: Dependency-aware multi-robot task decomposition (construction machinery)
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Own 3-level complexity benchmark
sota_methods.key_idea: A DAG of subtask dependencies. The authors report that explicit dependency modeling helps small models such as Llama-3.1-8B.
sota_methods.reported_results: DeepSeek-R1-671B gives the highest SR; Llama-3.1-8B gives the most reliable response time. No numbers were extracted.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Custom benchmark; no comparable public numbers.

benchmarks.name: PARTNR (Planning And Reasoning Tasks in humaN-Robot collaboration)
benchmarks.problem_class: 2-agent heterogeneous household rearrangement from language; spatial, temporal and capability constraints; partial observability; oracle or learned skills (Habitat 3.0)
benchmarks.metrics: Success rate, percent complete, sim steps, planning cycles, task offloading (human-in-the-loop)
benchmarks.baselines_included: ReAct single / centralized / decentralized, ReAct+RAG, fine-tuned 8B, heuristic expert
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Published numbers (ICLR 2025 Table 2); no leaderboard or eval server. Follow-ups: FLEET (2-agent subset, 0.59), LLawCo (PARTNR-Dialog, 74-75%)
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: Highest of the options: 1,000 test episodes, Meta-maintained, ICLR 2025, 100k training episodes for fine-tuning small models. Reviewers will accept it.
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: Medium-hard: Habitat-sim, GPU rendering and scene assets are needed. 4x H100 is ample for fine-tuning an 8B model.

benchmarks.name: PARTNR-Dialog
benchmarks.problem_class: PARTNR plus an explicit inter-agent message channel
benchmarks.metrics: Success rate
benchmarks.baselines_included: ReAct, CommPARTNR, LLawCo across 4 backbones
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Published numbers (ICML 2026): LLawCo 74-75% SR
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: Good if released, because it adds communication to a credible benchmark. Release status is unverified.
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: Same as PARTNR, if released

benchmarks.name: TDW-MAT and C-WAH (CoELA suite)
benchmarks.problem_class: Decentralized 2-agent embodied transport (ThreeDWorld) and household help (VirtualHome) with costly free-text communication
benchmarks.metrics: TDW-MAT: transport rate (with/without oracle perception). C-WAH: average steps (symbolic and visual observations).
benchmarks.baselines_included: RHP, CoRHP, MAT (RL), CoELA. External code: CoTS (MIT). CaPo code not released.
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Yes, a long chain of comparable tables: CoELA 71/85, CaPo 74/89, CoTS 83/93 (GPT-4, without/with oracle); C-WAH CoTS 81/49 steps
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: Widely used and accepted (ICLR, CVPR), but only 24 test episodes (TDW-MAT) and 10 tasks (C-WAH), so a gain of 2-4 points may be noise. SOTA numbers are GPT-4-dependent.
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: Hard: TDW and VirtualHome simulators, X server, Mask-RCNN perception

benchmarks.name: MAT-THOR
benchmarks.problem_class: Centralized heterogeneous multi-robot task allocation and planning from compound, complex or vague instructions (AI2-THOR)
benchmarks.metrics: SR, GCR (goal-condition recall), RU (robot utilization), executability, efficiency
benchmarks.baselines_included: LaMMA-P, SMART-LLM
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Published numbers: LaMMA-P 0.93 / 0.77 / 0.45; NEC hierarchical 0.95 / 0.84 / 0.60 (GPT-4o); KGLAMP with a different metric (GPT-5)
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: Moderate: ICRA 2025 lineage and several follow-ups, but only 70 tasks (30/20/20, 5 floor plans, 5 seeds). Numbers across papers are inconsistent, and communication is perfect, so a consensus allocator adds little on it.
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: Easy-medium: AI2-THOR, Python, Fast Downward

benchmarks.name: MAP-THOR
benchmarks.problem_class: Partially observable multi-agent household tasks with 4 instruction-ambiguity levels (AI2-THOR); 1-5 agents
benchmarks.metrics: Success, transport rate, coverage, balance, steps
benchmarks.baselines_included: Act, ReAct, CoT, SmartLLM, CoELA, LLaMAR
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Published: LLaMAR SR 0.66 (GPT-4V). No later method beating it on MAP-THOR was found.
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: Moderate: NeurIPS 2024 plus an ICML 2024 workshop benchmark paper. 45 tasks x 5 floor plans. GPT-4V is deprecated, so baselines must be re-run on a common backbone.
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: Easy-medium: AI2-THOR, MIT code

benchmarks.name: BoxNet1/2, Warehouse, BoxLift (HMAS-2 suite)
benchmarks.problem_class: Grid and box-moving coordination with growing agent counts; tests LLM communication architectures (CMAS, DMAS, HMAS)
benchmarks.metrics: Success rate, action steps, tokens and API calls
benchmarks.baselines_included: CMAS, DMAS, HMAS-1, HMAS-2
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: Low-moderate: ICRA 2024, but a toy 2D world with 2023-era GPT-4 baselines. Useful for scaling and token-cost claims.
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: Very easy: pure Python. The code calls the OpenAI API, but an open model could be swapped in.

benchmarks.name: CV_MRTA_Benchmark (decentralized MRTA under degraded communication)
benchmarks.license: No reuse license selected (README). Code is viewable, but redistribution and adaptation are not granted.
benchmarks.problem_class: Classical decentralized MRTA (no language) under Bernoulli, Gilbert-Elliott and Rayleigh loss; static and asynchronous online
benchmarks.metrics: MinMax, MinSum, viability, stability, publication intensity, redundancy, Gini, compute time
benchmarks.baselines_included: CBAA, ACBBA, PI, HIPC, DMCHBA, DGA
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Published: MinMax DGA 24.49; MinSum HIPC 66.95; HIPC and DMCHBA stable in all conditions
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: Low-moderate today: posted Sept 2026, no venue, one group. It is still the only public degraded-communication MRTA benchmark found.
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: Easy (Python and NumPy), but the licence issue must be resolved with the authors

benchmarks.name: COHERENT benchmark
benchmarks.problem_class: Heterogeneous (quadrotor, dog, arm) long-horizon tasks in BEHAVIOR-1K/OmniGibson; 100 tasks
benchmarks.metrics: Success rate, average steps
benchmarks.baselines_included: CMRS, DMRS variants, MCTS, LLM-MCTS, COHERENT
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Published: COHERENT 0.975 SR on 40 tasks
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: Low headroom (0.975). Heavy dependency on Isaac Sim 2022.2.
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: Hard

benchmarks.name: TeamCraft
benchmarks.problem_class: Multi-modal multi-agent Minecraft (building, clearing, farming, smelting); 55k task variants; tests generalization to new goals, scenes and agent counts
benchmarks.metrics: Task success, subgoal success
benchmarks.baselines_included: TeamCraft-VLA 7B/13B (centralized and decentralized), GPT-4o
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Published: 13B centralized 32-64% task success. GPT-4o fails almost all tasks. Venue: an ICLR 2025 submission was withdrawn; a NeurIPS 2025 D&B submission exists (acceptance not verified).
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: Moderate-low for MRTA: it mostly tests low-level VLA control and spatial grounding, not allocation.
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: Medium

benchmarks.name: MultiAgentBench (MARBLE)
benchmarks.problem_class: LLM multi-agent collaboration and competition across 6 textual scenarios; coordination topologies
benchmarks.metrics: Milestone-based task and coordination scores
benchmarks.baselines_included: Star, chain, tree and graph topologies; several LLMs
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Published (ACL 2025): gpt-4o-mini has the highest average task score; graph topology is best
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: Not embodied or robotic. Robotics reviewers would not accept it as MRTA SOTA.
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: Easy

open_gaps: No established LLM-embodied multi-agent benchmark models degraded links. MAT-THOR, MAP-THOR (centralized LLaMAR), PARTNR, COHERENT and TDW-MAT/C-WAH all assume lossless, instantaneous messages or central state. AgentComm-Bench (arXiv 2603.20285) stress-tests latency, loss and bandwidth, but it is a 20x20 grid world with classical strategies, no LLM agents and no allocation task, and no code was found. CV_MRTA (2609.13711) models loss but has no language. LDT-Coord (2607.09330) models path loss on only 3 RoCo tasks. So a SOTA claim 'under degraded communication' still has no accepted yardstick. That is why the CBJA testbed was not accepted as SOTA evidence, and it will recur unless results are also reported on the unmodified public benchmarks.

Latency and token cost are under-reported and often large. CoTS takes 26.8 s and about 7.9k characters per plan update. KGLAMP spends 181-301 s planning per task. EMOS uses about 80.8k tokens per episode. LLaMAR queries 4 LMs per step and admits higher cost. Efficiency-at-equal-success papers already exist: ELHPlan uses 30-40% of the tokens, CoBel-World cuts communication 64-79%, LDT-Coord 73-90x, OSDAG reasons 5-15x faster. A System-1 hybrid must therefore beat these on the success-vs-cost Pareto front, not merely be 'cheaper than GPT-4'.

Baseline numbers are inconsistent across papers. PARTNR reports decentralized ReAct at 0.73 SR, while FLEET's own setting gives 0.28. LaMMA-P self-reports 0.93/0.77/0.45 on MAT-THOR, KGLAMP's re-run is at least 25% lower, and EmboTeam reports 12% on MACE-THOR. CaPo's code is 'coming soon'. LLaMAR's GPT-4V backbone is discontinued. A credible SOTA claim needs same-backbone re-runs of the baselines, not copied numbers.

Test sets are small: TDW-MAT has 24 episodes, C-WAH 10 tasks, COHERENT 40 evaluated tasks, MACE-THOR 42 tasks, MAT-THOR 70 tasks (x5 seeds), MAP-THOR 45 tasks x 5 floor plans. Most reported SOTA margins of 2-4 points (CaPo over CoELA, LLawCo +4.5) come without confidence intervals. PARTNR (1,000 test episodes) is the exception, and the only place a small but real gain would be statistically defensible.

Strong non-LLM or heuristic coordination is under-credited. On TDW-MAT the heuristic pair CoRHP scores 61 without oracle and 75 with oracle, above every GPT-3.5 LLM agent without oracle (52-59). On PARTNR the privileged Heuristic-Expert reaches 0.84 SR in 1,261 steps, against 0.73-0.74 and 1,347-3,295 steps for LLM planners. Structured allocation plus a small model may close much of the gap; nobody has published a consensus-auction coordinator on these benchmarks (no such paper found in search).

Free-text dialogue is an inefficient and sometimes harmful coordination channel. Dongre & Hakkani-Tür (arXiv 2605.12920) find that adding dialogue on PARTNR cuts action conflicts by 40-83 points yet lowers task success compared with silent coordination. Fully decentralized dialogue (DMAS) collapses in HMAS-2 (0-25% on BoxNet1, BoxNet2 and Warehouse). Compact, structured bid and claim messages as in CBBA are an untested alternative on these benchmarks.

Scaling beyond 2-3 agents is barely evaluated. PARTNR, TDW-MAT, C-WAH and MAP-THOR (main) use 2 agents. TeamCraft models degrade severely at 4 agents. HMAS-2 shows centralized LLM planning scales worst. DynaHMRC (2606.14882) cites a context bottleneck. Consensus allocators routinely handle 10-24 robots and 50-100 tasks, which is a natural advantage for the hybrid if a credible many-agent benchmark is used.

Dynamic mid-mission changes (new or revised instructions, capability loss, notices lifting or imposing constraints) appear only in custom benchmarks: KGLAMP replanning, CoMuRoS, DynaHMRC, the CBJA testbed. No standardized public benchmark was found for language constraints that change during execution.

Allocation is not the only bottleneck. On PARTNR, SR falls from 0.73 (oracle skills) to 0.57 (learned skills) to 0.30 (learned skills + ConceptGraph perception), and the paper names task-tracking and recovery failures. Any allocation-centric method must report on the oracle-skill track and state this ceiling honestly, or it will be attacked for claiming 'SOTA' on a component that does not dominate end-to-end success.

Fine-tuned small models already rival large ones where training data exists. PARTNR's fine-tuned 8B matches a 70B model at 8.6x faster inference, and LLawCo fine-tunes Qwen-3-14B to 74%. This supports the CBJA paper's own finding that judge quality matters more than query selection. It also means 'small fast model' alone is not novel; novelty has to come from how the small model's outputs feed a decentralized allocator.

sota_opportunities.idea: Consensus-claimed subtask allocation plus a fine-tuned small on-board planner. The LLM extracts PARTNR's task graph (subtasks, precedence, capability constraints) once. Each robot's fine-tuned 8B 'System-1' model scores feasibility and utility bids for subtasks from its partial observation. A CBBA-style bid/claim consensus replaces free-text ReAct coordination, which removes duplicated work and gives explicit task tracking. The slow LLM is called only for graph extraction and failure recovery.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: PARTNR, decentralized, oracle skills, partial observability (1,000 test episodes). Secondary: PARTNR-Dialog if released, and a message-loss variant reported as extra analysis, never replacing the standard track.
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: ReAct decentralized 0.73 SR / 3,295 sim steps / 15.24 planning cycles. Finetuned-8B 0.70 / 3,229 / 12.85. Centralized ReAct 0.74 (partial obs). LLawCo 74-75% (PARTNR-Dialog). FLEET 0.59 on its 2-agent subset. Human-level reference 0.93; privileged heuristic 0.84 / 1,261 steps.
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: The PARTNR paper names poor coordination and task-tracking failures as the main LLM weakness. Decentralized planners take 2.4x the steps of the privileged heuristic. Published follow-ups (LLawCo, dialogue-alignment work) improve the LLM's reasoning or messages, but none replaces coordination with a consensus auction. 100k training episodes plus 4x H100 make fine-tuning an 8B System-1 feasible.
sota_opportunities.risk: Habitat 3.0 setup cost. Success is capped by skill and perception failures (0.57 and 0.30 on the learned tracks), so the realistic claim is 'equal-or-better SR at markedly fewer sim steps, planning cycles and wall-clock', and SR gains may be within 1-2 points. Two-agent teams limit how much allocation can add. PARTNR-Dialog release is unverified.

sota_opportunities.idea: A structured claim protocol with a small System-1 intent/belief classifier on TDW-MAT and C-WAH. Agents exchange compact bids and claims (target object, container, ETA) rather than LLM dialogue. A fine-tuned small model predicts the teammate's intent and when an LLM replan is needed, and the LLM is invoked only on predicted conflicts. Report success and cost as a Pareto front (transport rate vs LLM calls, characters, wall-clock), using an open-weight backbone for every method.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: TDW-MAT (with and without oracle perception) and C-WAH (symbolic and visual)
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: Without oracle, GPT-4: CoTS 83, CaPo 74, CoELA 71. With oracle: CoTS 93, CaPo 89. Non-LLM CoRHP: 61 / 75. C-WAH steps: CoTS 81 / 49. Communication: CoBel-World (-64-79% versus CoELA and CaPo). Tokens: ELHPlan (30-40% of SoTA).
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: Every method since CoELA coordinates by free-text LLM dialogue: CoTS costs 26.8 s per plan update and CaPo 14-17 updates per task. The heuristic CoRHP is already competitive, which suggests structured coordination plus a small model could match GPT-4 dialogue at a fraction of the cost. No consensus-auction coordinator has been reported on these benchmarks.
sota_opportunities.risk: Only 24 and 10 test episodes, so claims need many seeds and CIs and remain fragile. Beating CoTS's GPT-4 numbers outright is unlikely without a strong LLM. The realistic claim is SOTA at a given open-weight backbone and cost budget. TDW and VirtualHome are painful to install. CaPo has no code, so it cannot be re-run.

sota_opportunities.idea: LLM front end, decentralized optimizing allocation back end, small verifier. The LLM produces a task DAG and a capability matrix once. A decentralized consensus allocator such as CBBA or GACA-style group bidding replaces the prompted allocation or central MILP. A fine-tuned small System-1 verifies feasibility of the action and PDDL preconditions before execution and triggers local replanning.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: MAT-THOR (compound, complex, vague) and MAP-THOR; optionally MACE-THOR
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: MAT-THOR SR: NEC hierarchical 0.95 / 0.84 / 0.60, LaMMA-P 0.93 / 0.77 / 0.45 (GPT-4o). KGLAMP TCR 84.0 / 68.4 / 71.4 (GPT-5, different metric). MAP-THOR: LLaMAR SR 0.66 / TR 0.91 (GPT-4V, which must be re-run). MACE-THOR: EmboTeam 55% SR.
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: The 'vague' category (0.60) and MAP-THOR (0.66) still have headroom. Allocation in these pipelines is prompted or centralized. FLEET shows that swapping LLM allocation for an optimizer gives large gains on heterogeneous and temporal tasks (0.28 to 0.59). KGLAMP planning takes minutes, which leaves room for a much faster pipeline.
sota_opportunities.risk: Vague-command gains mostly depend on the LLM's disambiguation, which a small System-1 will not fix. With perfect communication and 2-4 robots a decentralized consensus layer adds nothing over a central solver, so reviewers will ask why decentralize. The benchmarks are small (70 and 45x5 tasks). The NEC paper already reaches RU 1.00. This is best framed as a secondary result, not the main SOTA claim.
sota_opportunities.evidence_urls: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.20560 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21670 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04129 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.10031 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.11063 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07417

sota_opportunities.idea: Many-agent scaling with a small System-1 and consensus. Run the hybrid against LLM communication architectures as the team grows to 16-32 agents, where central and dialogue-based LLM coordination breaks on context length and token cost.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: HMAS-2 suite (BoxNet1/2, Warehouse, BoxLift), extended agent counts
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: HMAS-2 82.5 / 57.5 / 62.5 / 100 SR; CMAS 75 / 27.5 / 15 / 90 (GPT-4). Code-as-Symbolic-Planner (IROS 2025) reports +24.1% over the best baselines across 7 TAMP tasks; its per-task BoxNet numbers are unverified.
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: The HMAS-2 paper shows success collapsing for centralized and decentralized LLM dialogue as agents are added. Consensus auctions are built for this regime, and the suite is pure Python (MIT), so iteration is fast.
sota_opportunities.risk: A toy 2D world with 2023-era GPT-4 baselines; reviewers may discount it as SOTA evidence. Newer methods such as Code-as-Symbolic-Planner may already be ahead. Use it as a supporting scalability study, not the headline.

sota_opportunities.idea: A loss-adaptive consensus allocator: bundle length and rebroadcast chosen online from estimated link quality (the companion paper shows the best bundle length shifts from 12 to 2 under 25% loss), optionally with RL-learned bids. Evaluate on the only public degraded-communication MRTA benchmark, then add language-gated task permissions as an extension, reusing the CBJA judges.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: CV_MRTA_Benchmark (Bernoulli, Gilbert-Elliott and Rayleigh; MinMax and MinSum; viability and stability)
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: MinMax: DGA 24.49, DMCHBA 24.78. MinSum: HIPC 66.95, DGA 67.22. Stability: HIPC and DMCHBA are stable in all 25 conditions. Compute: DMCHBA 4.88 ms. GACA reports about 97% optimality vs 81-84% for CBBA (not on this benchmark).
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: No allocator in that benchmark wins every metric: DGA is best on MinMax but becomes unstable, HIPC is stable but not best on MinMax. Bundle length is fixed per run although its optimum depends on loss. This matches the researcher's CBBA and degraded-communication expertise directly.
sota_opportunities.risk: Published Sept 2026 with no venue, so it is not yet an 'established' benchmark. The code has no reuse license, and permission is needed. It has no language component, so the System-1 story weakens. Best positioned as the communication-robustness pillar next to a headline PARTNR or TDW-MAT result.

sweeps.area: Decentralized multi-robot task allocation and coordination for group missions under degraded or intermittent communication. Covers CBBA-family auctions and consensus, consensus-free and event-triggered execution, MARL with learned communication, exploration under limited communication, and LLM-based cooperative embodied agents. Snapshot date 2026-09-27. The session's web-search budget (200 calls) ran out before the sweep finished; everything after that point was checked with WebFetch, curl or git clone. Key finding, computed in this session: I reproduced the only public degraded-communication MRTA benchmark (CV_MRTA_Benchmark, Lott & Honary, Sep 2026). My pipeline matches the paper's published means exactly (DGA 24.49, DMCHBA 24.78, HIPC MinSum 66.95). I then solved all 500 instances to exact optimality with Held-Karp plus subset-partition DP, using the Manhattan relaxation that ignores collisions; no run among 150,000 beats this bound. Averaged over the impaired conditions, the best published method is 24.6% above optimum on MinMax (24.49 vs 19.65) and 35.7% above on MinSum (66.95 vs 49.33). In the worst condition, even the best method per condition reaches 1.49x (MinMax) and 1.80x (MinSum). The instances are static and fully determined by the shared config, so I infer that a planner every robot runs locally with no negotiation would reach this optimum without any allocation messages. That makes the benchmark close to degenerate as a test of communication robustness.
