sota_methods.name: DGA / DMCHBA / HIPC (the best published allocators on CV_MRTA_Benchmark)
sota_methods.problem: Decentralized MRTA, Collaborative Visit task: 4 robots, 10 known targets, 19x19 grid. Tested under ideal communication and 3 loss families (Bernoulli, Gilbert-Elliott, Rayleigh) at 8 severities.
sota_methods.key_idea: Six non-learning allocators run in one shared event-driven simulator: CBAA, ACBBA, PI, HIPC, DMCHBA (clone-based matching) and DGA (decentralized evolutionary team-plan search).
sota_methods.benchmark_used: CV_MRTA_Benchmark: 500 paired instances x 25 communication conditions
sota_methods.reported_results: Mean MinMax over impaired conditions: DGA 24.49, DMCHBA 24.78 steps. Best MinSum: HIPC 66.95. Fewest messages: DMCHBA, 2.08 publications per team step. Compute: DMCHBA 4.88 ms vs DGA 1.346 s. My exact-optimum check: optimum means are 19.65 (MinMax) and 49.33 (MinSum). Best-algorithm ratio to optimum: Bernoulli average 1.23 (DGA MinMax) and 1.39 (HIPC MinSum); at p=0.7, 1.36 and 1.70. Under ideal communication, DGA hits the MinMax optimum on only 38.2% of instances.
sota_methods.license: No license declared (GitHub API returns none; a CITATION.cff is present)
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Very small scale. All instances are static and fully known, so a planner replicated on every robot needs no negotiation. The benchmark is brand-new with no community uptake (0 stars). The paper's Pareto trade-off means no single method dominates.

sota_methods.name: CC-OPI (Communication-Constrained Online Performance Impact)
sota_methods.problem: Online distributed task allocation for UAV swarms whose short communication range splits them into transient information islands. Tasks have deadlines, capacities and runtime arrivals.
sota_methods.key_idea: Event-driven: negotiation is interleaved with execution. Uses a spatial-locality penalty, a deadline-urgency term and a non-preemptive state lock, and terminates in finite time without stale-completion deadlock.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Own simulator: 10 km x 10 km field, N in {6..16} UAVs, M = 2N or 3N tasks, Rc = 250 m. 30 seeds plus 30 hold-out seeds, bootstrap 95% CIs.
sota_methods.reported_results: Task completion rate (TCR) about 0.80, roughly flat across scale. About +7 pp over matched online PI-OM/CBBA-OM and about +20 pp over naively transferred allocate-then-execute baselines. Within a few pp of PI/CBBA under full connectivity.
sota_methods.code_url: https://github.com/bdathe-lb/CC-OPI-Exp (link given in the arXiv abstract, but HTTP 404 on 2026-09-27)
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Code not public. Assumes synchronized clocks and reliable delivery within range. No agent failures, no energy limits, straight-line motion. Headroom: even the full-connectivity reference is only about 0.8 TCR.

sota_methods.name: GACA (Grouping Auction-Consensus Algorithm)
sota_methods.problem: Decentralized MinSum MRTA (multi-task robots, single-robot tasks) under ideal communication.
sota_methods.key_idea: Agents bid on groups of spatially nearby tasks (claim, acquire or contest a group) instead of single tasks, and consensus resolves the group actions.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: 4,000 random worlds (5-20 agents, 10-50 tasks) plus 3,280 scalability instances, scored against a MILP optimum (PuLP)
sota_methods.reported_results: Median percent-optimality about 97% for GACA vs 81-84% for CBBA, with equal or fewer convergence iterations.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: The authors state that robustness to imperfect communication was not tested; everything assumes a fully connected graph. No code.

sota_methods.name: FORMICA (decision-focused communication-free MRTA)
sota_methods.problem: Task allocation with zero robot-to-robot communication.
sota_methods.key_idea: Each robot predicts its teammates' bids. The predictors are trained to minimize Task Allocation Regret (Smart Predict-then-Optimize) rather than prediction error, with a mean-field approximation that cuts cost from O(NT) to O(T).
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Own scenarios: 16 robots / 64 tasks, and 256 robots / 4,096 tasks
sota_methods.reported_results: +17% system reward over the analytical mean-field baseline at 16/64, approaching the MILP optimum. +7% at 256/4096. About 21 s of training on a laptop.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Its only baseline is an analytical predictor, with no comparison to CBBA-family methods under partial communication. Evidence that learned implicit coordination can replace consensus, but it has not been combined with sparse communication.

sota_methods.name: ED-CBBA (Event-Driven CBBA)
sota_methods.problem: Keep CBBA quality while sending fewer messages in communication-limited settings.
sota_methods.key_idea: Event-triggered rebroadcast in place of periodic consensus, with convergence guarantees kept.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Own Monte Carlo runs varying agents, targets and bundle size
sota_methods.reported_results: Up to 52% fewer messages at quality equivalent to CBBA.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Improves messages only, not quality. Loss robustness not the focus.

sota_methods.name: AC-DMTA (Assignment-Consistent Dynamic Multi-UAV Task Allocation)
sota_methods.problem: Dynamic multi-UAV allocation when information is stale and asymmetric.
sota_methods.key_idea: Stale records are modeled as uncertainty sets and bids become interval bids. Task-winner and bundle-stability certificates suppress messages that cannot change the assignment.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Own simulation. Reported baselines: periodic CBBA, ED-CBBA, C-CBBA, TLC-CBBA.
sota_methods.reported_results: Large reductions in communication were claimed; I could not read the exact numbers.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: MDPI venue with lower reviewer credibility. The full text returned HTTP 403, so the details come only from the abstract seen in a search snippet.

sota_methods.name: CommFormer
sota_methods.problem: Learning the communication graph in cooperative MARL.
sota_methods.key_idea: The communication architecture is a learnable graph, optimized by bi-level gradient descent with continuous relaxation, on an attention-based encoder-decoder (MAT-style).
sota_methods.benchmark_used: SMAC, Predator-Prey, Predator-Capture-Prey, GRF
sota_methods.reported_results: SMAC win rates at sparsity 0.4: 100% on most maps; 5m_vs_6m 89.6; 27m_vs_30m 96.9; 3s5z_vs_3s6z 87.5. Beats MAT, MAPPO, HAPPO and QMIX.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: SMAC v1 is saturated. Channels are assumed perfect: no evaluation under dropout or delay.

sota_methods.name: ExpoComm
sota_methods.problem: Scalable communication for many-agent MARL.
sota_methods.key_idea: Exponential-graph topology with small diameter for fast dissemination, plus memory-based message processors and auxiliary grounding tasks. Cost is near-linear in N.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: MAgent, Infrastructure Management Planning (IMP)
sota_methods.reported_results: Claims better performance and zero-shot transfer across agent counts than prior communication methods (exact numbers not extracted).
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Topology is fixed and assumes delivery. No lossy-channel evaluation. Not task allocation.

sota_methods.name: MARO / Value-Aware MARO (hybrid execution under communication dropout)
sota_methods.venue: Value-Aware MARO: IROS 2026 (per arXiv). MARO (arXiv 2210.06274): venue not confirmed.
sota_methods.problem: Keep MARL performance at arbitrary communication levels.
sota_methods.key_idea: A centrally trained autoregressive predictor fills in missing teammate observations at run time. The value-aware version weights the predictor loss by advantage.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: MPE with varying communication reliability
sota_methods.reported_results: More than 20% mean-return improvement and 64.7% less variance when communication success is below 40% (Value-Aware MARO vs MARO). MARO reportedly beats baselines in 22 of 24 scenarios (search snippet only).
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Tested only on MPE-scale tasks; no SMACv2 or robotics allocation. The key idea (predict what you did not receive) has not been brought to MRTA consensus.

sota_methods.name: IR2 (Implicit Rendezvous)
sota_methods.problem: Time-sensitive multi-robot exploration under sparse, intermittent connectivity.
sota_methods.key_idea: Attention-based deep RL with curriculum learning and hierarchical graphs; trades off solo exploration against reconnecting to share information.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Three Gazebo worlds (indoor 130x100 m, forest 150x150 m, campus 340x340 m)
sota_methods.reported_results: 6.6-34.1% shorter exploration paths than pursuit-based and preplanned rendezvous baselines.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Each paper uses its own worlds, so there is no shared leaderboard. Baselines are weak (heuristics).

sota_methods.name: MACE (Adaptive Communication Windows)
sota_methods.problem: Communication-constrained exploration in which robots decide whether a communication window is worth the detour.
sota_methods.key_idea: Evaluates communication cost at scheduled windows and routes each robot through a Vehicle Orienteering Problem variant.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Own simulated environments
sota_methods.reported_results: Up to 23% less total exploration time than opportunistic and fixed-rendezvous strategies.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: No code. Own environments.

sota_methods.name: CaPo (Cooperative Plan Optimization)
sota_methods.problem: Two LLM agents cooperating on long-horizon embodied tasks where communication is costly.
sota_methods.key_idea: The agents first discuss a meta-plan, then adapt it to progress while executing.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: TDW-MAT and C-WAH (introduced by CoELA, ICLR 2024)
sota_methods.reported_results: TDW-MAT transport rate with GPT-4: 74% without oracle perception (CoELA 71, RoCo 71, ProAgent 69) and 89% with oracle (CoELA 85). With GPT-3.5 and oracle: 84 vs CoELA 72. C-WAH average steps with GPT-4 (lower is better): symbolic 51 vs CoELA 57; visual 83 vs 92.
sota_methods.license: paper CC BY 4.0; code license not checked
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Only 2 agents. Messages are costly but never lost or delayed. Depends on the GPT-4 API.

sota_methods.name: Dec-MCTS
sota_methods.problem: Decentralized multi-robot planning for active perception under lossy communication.
sota_methods.key_idea: Each robot runs MCTS, periodically broadcasts compressed search trees, and updates a product distribution over joint plans by variational optimization.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Own active-perception and orienteering scenarios
sota_methods.reported_results: Per the abstract (search snippet): no significant degradation at 50% packet loss; at 97% loss it is degraded but still better than no communication.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Older. The publisher page returned 403, so the claims come from a snippet. A strong conceptual baseline for plans that remain robust to loss.

sota_methods.name: CA-CBBA (Communication-Aware CBBA)
sota_methods.problem: CBBA when bandwidth is limited and messages collide.
sota_methods.key_idea: A deep-RL policy learns which agents transmit and when (self-censoring) so that mission-critical bids get priority on the shared channel.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Own simulation
sota_methods.reported_results: Not extracted (the MIT DSpace PDF returned 405).
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Seen only in search listings. The closest precedent for 'learned value of communication inside CBBA', which the researcher's CBJA VOC work overlaps.

benchmarks.name: CV_MRTA_Benchmark (Collaborative Visit under degraded communication)
benchmarks.problem_class: Decentralized MRTA with lossy communication: 4 robots, 10 known targets, 19x19 grid, Bernoulli / Gilbert-Elliott / Rayleigh loss at 8 severities plus ideal. Static targets, known at start.
benchmarks.metrics: Realized MinMax (max robot steps), MinSum (team steps), messages per completed target, allocation reliability, allocator compute time
benchmarks.baselines_included: CBAA, ACBBA, PI, HIPC, DMCHBA, DGA, all in pure Python behind one event-driven robot shell
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Yes: per-trial records for 100,000 asynchronous missions plus published summary numbers. I reproduced the paper means exactly.
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: High. Standard-library simulator, pip install, smoke tests; a new allocator plugs into the common robot shell.
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: Low to moderate. Brand-new (Sep 2026), 0 stars, tiny scale. Near-degenerate for testing communication robustness: I solved all 500 instances exactly, and the best published methods sit 24.6% (MinMax) and 35.7% (MinSum) above optimum. Because the instances are static and fully known, a planner replicated on each robot would need no allocation messages. Good for a sanity win, not enough on its own.

benchmarks.name: Nayak et al. 2020 comparison protocol (RA-L 5(2):572-579)
benchmarks.problem_class: Decentralized task allocation under imperfect communication, in two scenarios: collaborative visit (known targets) and collaborative search-and-visit (unknown targets).
benchmarks.metrics: Maximum distance travelled by any agent; maximum messages sent by any agent
benchmarks.baselines_included: CBAA, ACBBA, DHBA, HIPC, PI under Bernoulli, Gilbert-Elliott and Rayleigh fading
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Published numbers in the paper (not extracted here)
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: Medium. The protocol is well specified and CV_MRTA reuses its communication models, but the search-and-visit scenario would have to be reimplemented.
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: Moderate: an RA-L paper from Otte's group, the de-facto reference protocol. Search-and-visit involves private, dynamic information, which is the regime that actually matters.

benchmarks.name: CC-OPI online UAV-swarm scenario
benchmarks.problem_class: Online MRTA with deadlines, capacities, heterogeneous UAVs, 250 m communication radius, packet loss, terrain occlusion and runtime task arrivals.
benchmarks.metrics: Task completion rate (TCR) over reachable tasks, makespan, distance, wasted distance, reassignments, messages per completed task, emergency rescue rate
benchmarks.baselines_included: PI, CBBA, PI-MaxAss (full connectivity and naive transfer), PI-OM and CBBA-OM (matched online), GEO (Voronoi)
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Yes, published tables: TCR about 0.80 for CC-OPI at 250 m with 30 seeds plus 30 hold-out seeds
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: Low to medium. The parameters are fully specified in the paper, but it must be reimplemented until the code is released.
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: Moderate if the code is released; otherwise reviewers will question reimplementation fidelity. Has clear headroom (TCR about 0.8).

benchmarks.name: SMACv2, plus a communication-dropout protocol
benchmarks.problem_class: Cooperative MARL under partial observability; the communication-dropout protocol must be self-defined (MARO-style).
benchmarks.metrics: Win rate or return as a function of message-delivery probability and bandwidth
benchmarks.baselines_included: MAPPO, QMIX, MAT (native). Communication methods (CommFormer, MAGIC, TarMAC, IC3Net) must be ported.
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Yes for the environment (NeurIPS 2023 Datasets & Benchmarks). No for a standard lossy-communication variant.
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: Medium. Needs StarCraft II; 4x H100 is ample.
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: High for the environment, low for any custom dropout protocol. SMAC v1 is saturated (CommFormer reaches 100% on most maps).

benchmarks.name: RoboCup Rescue Agent Simulation (RCRS)
benchmarks.problem_class: Heterogeneous disaster-response teams (fire brigades, police, ambulances) that must allocate tasks over channel-based radio and voice communication with bandwidth limits and dropout/failure noise.
benchmarks.metrics: Official competition score (civilian health and survival, building damage), summed across maps
benchmarks.baselines_included: ADF sample agents in Java and Python, and a DCOP module (uiiaoo/dcop.rrs-adf)
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Competition results: 2025 final Timrad 63, AIT-Rescue 58, 3Rakshak 48. I verified that the shipped comm profiles include degraded settings, e.g. sakae comms-03-midle (channel failure p=0.2, output dropout p=0.1), plus low, none and jammer profiles.
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: Low. A Java ecosystem with a steep learning curve. I could not find an archive of team code from 2023-2025.
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: Moderate to high as an established external benchmark with built-in degraded communication, but uncommon at ML and robotics venues. Scores vary by year and map set.

benchmarks.name: TDW-MAT / C-WAH (CoELA suite)
benchmarks.problem_class: LLM-driven cooperative embodied agents with costly natural-language communication
benchmarks.metrics: Transport rate (TDW-MAT), average steps (C-WAH), communication counts and token usage
benchmarks.baselines_included: MHP, RHP, CoELA, ProAgent, RoCo, CaPo
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Yes, published tables (CaPo ICLR 2025: 89% transport rate with oracle perception and GPT-4)
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: Medium. ThreeDWorld plus LLM API costs.
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: High in the LLM-agent community, but only 2 agents, no message loss or latency, and dominated by GPT-4-class models. Poor fit for small System-1 models if the goal is to beat SOTA.

benchmarks.name: POGEMA
benchmarks.problem_class: Decentralized, partially observable (lifelong) multi-agent pathfinding
benchmarks.metrics: Success rate, sum of costs, throughput, plus cooperation, out-of-distribution and scalability metrics
benchmarks.baselines_included: LaCAM, RHCR, DCC, SCRIMP, Follower, MATS-LP, MAMBA. MAPF-GPT (AAAI 2025) and MAPF-GPT-DDG (IROS 2025) are in separate repos.
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Raw evaluation data plus paper tables. No live leaderboard.
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: High (pip, fast)
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: High for decentralized coordination, but it covers pathfinding rather than allocation and has no model of communication degradation.

benchmarks.name: SAREnv
benchmarks.problem_class: Multi-UAV wilderness search and rescue coverage over 60 geospatial scenarios with lost-person probability maps
benchmarks.metrics: Accumulated and time-discounted probability of detection, discovery score
benchmarks.baselines_included: Spiral / Concentric Circles, Pizza Zigzag, Greedy, Random
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Paper tables
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: High
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: Low to moderate. Weak baselines and no communication modeling, so a communication layer would have to be added.

open_gaps: No community-accepted benchmark exists for decentralized MRTA under degraded communication. Nayak et al. 2020 (RA-L) has no public code. CV_MRTA_Benchmark (Sep 2026) is public but tiny: 4 robots, 10 targets, 19x19 grid. CC-OPI's code link returns 404. Every paper, including the researcher's CBJA, builds its own testbed, which is exactly why the earlier SOTA claim failed.

The public benchmark is nearly degenerate (computed here). Targets and start layout are fixed and shared, so each robot could solve the joint problem exactly with no negotiation. The best published allocators still sit 24.6% (MinMax) and 35.7% (MinSum) above optimum when averaged over impaired conditions, and in the worst condition even the best method per condition reaches 1.49x and 1.80x. Communication robustness only means something when information is private and changes over time: target discovery, runtime arrivals, failures, local observations.

Solution quality falls short even under perfect communication. GACA reports CBBA at 81-84% median optimality versus 97% for grouped bidding, but GACA was never tested under loss and has no code. Under ideal communication DGA reaches the MinMax optimum on only 38% of CV instances and HIPC the MinSum optimum on 28%.

The online regime with a fragmented network is far from solved. CC-OPI reaches only about 0.80 task completion rate (TCR) at a 250 m radius, and even the full-connectivity PI/CBBA reference is close to that. Its assumptions (synchronized clocks, reliable delivery within range, no failures) leave obvious stress axes untested.

Two families never meet. Communication-free implicit coordination (FORMICA predicts teammates' bids and approaches the MILP optimum with zero messages; SwarmCF recovers about 80% of centralized performance) and communication-efficient consensus (ED-CBBA -52% messages; AC-DMTA certificates; event-triggered consensus) are not combined. No method predicts what was lost and communicates only when the prediction would change the assignment.

Papers on message efficiency report message counts or solution quality in isolation. None reports quality at matched bandwidth across a loss-severity sweep, which is the Pareto frontier a SOTA claim should be made on.

Learned-communication MARL (CommFormer, ExpoComm, MAGIC, TarMAC, IC3Net) assumes perfect channels. Dropout robustness appears only in MARO and Value-Aware MARO, tested on MPE-scale tasks. SMAC v1 is saturated (CommFormer at 100% on most maps), and there is no standard lossy-communication protocol for SMACv2 or VMAS.
Exploration under limited communication (IR2, MACE, rendezvous as job-shop scheduling, RACER) has no shared worlds or leaderboard. MACE, the newest (Sep 2026), has no code.

LLM cooperative-agent benchmarks (TDW-MAT, C-WAH) charge a cost for communication but never drop or delay messages. They have only 2 agents and depend on GPT-4, so they are a poor venue for a small on-board 'System-1' model to claim SOTA.

Lesson for this research line: CBJA found that VOC query selection was statistically equivalent to a simple incremental deadline rule. The measurable SOTA margin is therefore in allocation quality and consistency under loss and partitions, not in the language gate, which should be treated as one source of private information rather than the core claim.

sota_opportunities.idea: PRIMARY: Replicated-Plan Consensus (RPC). Every robot runs the same deterministic anytime joint planner (exact DP or MILP for small N, otherwise LNS or LKH with a shared seed) on its current belief of the shared world. Only planner inputs are communicated (robot states and discovered or completed tasks), with redundant low-rate gossip. A divergence certificate, in the spirit of AC-DMTA's interval bids, triggers extra messages only when a belief change could alter the robot's own assignment. When messages are missing, a learned teammate predictor (FORMICA or MARO style, trained on 4x H100) fills in the gaps. Iterative bid consensus is dropped entirely.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: Step 1: CV_MRTA_Benchmark, all 25 conditions, against the 6 published allocators and their released per-trial records. Step 2: a private-information 'search-and-visit' variant following Nayak et al. 2020, contributed back to the same repo so every baseline runs unchanged.
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: MinMax: DGA 24.49 (impaired mean), DMCHBA 24.78, HIPC 25.12. MinSum: HIPC 66.95, DGA 85.18. Exact optima: 19.65 and 49.33. Worst-condition best ratios: 1.49x (MinMax) and 1.80x (MinSum). Messages: DMCHBA about 187 sent per mission.
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: Every published method uses iterative consensus that needs many consistent rounds, and loss breaks those rounds. Nobody exploits the fact that replicated deterministic planning needs only consistent inputs, which cheap redundant state gossip provides even at p=0.7 loss. Expected result: at most 1.05x optimum in every condition with fewer allocation messages, a 15-40% margin.
sota_opportunities.risk: On the static known-visit task, reviewers will call the win trivial because the benchmark is degenerate. That result should be presented as a finding about the benchmark, and the SOTA claim should rest on the private-information and dynamic variant. Scaling beyond about 20 robots needs an approximate planner, and deterministic replicas can still diverge when beliefs differ.

sota_opportunities.idea: Take RPC with learned teammate prediction into the fragmented-network online regime (runtime arrivals, deadlines, information islands). Robots in one island plan jointly over a predicted belief of what the other islands are doing. They communicate only 'surprise' events (task completed or claimed, new task, failure) and re-merge plans when islands rejoin.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: The CC-OPI scenario rebuilt from its paper spec: 10 km field, N 6-16, M = 2N or 3N, Rc = 250 m, deadlines U[0,1200] s, packet loss and occlusion, 30 dev seeds plus 30 hold-out seeds, bootstrap CIs. Also a sweep of Rc and added UAV failures, which CC-OPI does not model.
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: CC-OPI TCR about 0.80, PI-OM and CBBA-OM about 0.73 (about -7 pp), GEO Voronoi, naive PI-C / CBBA-C about 0.60 (about -20 pp). Aim for at least 0.88 TCR at an equal or lower message count per completed task.
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: CC-OPI coordinates implicitly through local penalties but does not predict teammates' intentions across islands. Even full-connectivity PI/CBBA stays near 0.8, so allocation quality under deadlines, not only communication, is the bottleneck.
sota_opportunities.risk: The CC-OPI code is unreleased (404), so reimplementation fidelity can be disputed. Mitigation: publish the full reimplementation, match the reported CC-OPI numbers within CI before claiming gains, and ask the authors for their code.

sota_opportunities.idea: A near-optimal learned allocator that holds up under loss. Distil a MILP or LKH joint planner into a permutation-equivariant transformer or GNN policy that runs on each robot's belief state (not on received bids). Train it with Bernoulli, Gilbert-Elliott, Rayleigh and partition dropout, and report percent-optimality against MILP.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: GACA's instance protocol (5-20 agents, 10-50 tasks, random square worlds, MILP ground truth) extended with the three CV_MRTA loss models, and with robot states made private so the task is not degenerate.
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: CBBA 81-84% median optimality with ideal communication; GACA about 97% with ideal communication (reimplementation needed). CBBA with a learned bidding scheme (Rodriguez et al., arXiv 2605.21932). DGA and HIPC from the CV_MRTA code.
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: GACA explicitly left imperfect communication untested, and the learned-bidding CBBA work likewise does not test communication degradation. No published method reports percent-optimality as a function of loss. A target of at least 95% median optimality at 50% Bernoulli loss would be a clear margin.
sota_opportunities.risk: No code for GACA or the learned-bidding paper, so both need reimplementation. Static instances slide back toward degeneracy unless states are kept private.

sota_opportunities.idea: Secondary, for external validity: a communication-robust allocation module for RoboCup Rescue. Drop the RPC or learned allocator into the ADF target-allocator slots for fire brigades, police and ambulances, and evaluate on the official degraded comm profiles (low, none, jammer).
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: RCRS official maps (e.g. sakae, paris) with the shipped comms-0x profiles
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: ADF sample team, the DCOP module (dcop.rrs-adf), and past competition teams (2025 final: Timrad 63, AIT-Rescue 58) where binaries or code are available
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: An established simulator with built-in dropout, failure and bandwidth noise, yet the published work consists of competition reports and small-venue papers with no learned or replicated-planning allocators under the degraded profiles.
sota_opportunities.risk: Heavy Java engineering. I could not locate archived 2023-2025 team code, and scores are not comparable across years. ML reviewers may not recognize the benchmark.

sota_opportunities.idea: Alternative MARL track: CommFormer-style learned graph communication combined with a MARO-style predictor of missing messages and dropout-curriculum training. Evaluate as return versus delivery probability versus bandwidth budget.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: SMACv2 and VMAS (BenchMARL) with a released lossy-communication wrapper
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: CommFormer (ICLR 2024), MAGIC (AAMAS 2021), TarMAC, IC3Net, ExpoComm (ICLR 2025), MARO / Value-Aware MARO (IROS 2026), MAPPO and QMIX without communication
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: The strongest communication methods were never evaluated under dropout, and the dropout-robust methods were evaluated only on MPE.
sota_opportunities.risk: A crowded field with small margins, and the lossy protocol is self-defined, which is the same credibility problem as before. It is also distant from the researcher's CBBA and System-1 strengths.

sweeps.area: Multi-robot / multi-agent group-mission allocation and routing treated as optimization. The sweep covers OR state of the art (HGS, PyVRP, SISR, ALNS) for VRPTW, the team orienteering problem (TOP/TOPTW), dynamic VRPTW with stochastic arrivals, the dynamic team orienteering problem (DTOP) and min-max mTSP, set against decentralized CBBA-family allocators under degraded communication. Checked on 2026-09-27. The WebSearch budget (200 calls) ran out near the end, so "not found" below means not found in this sweep. It does not prove the work is absent.

sota_methods.name: HGS-CVRP (Hybrid Genetic Search with SWAP*)
sota_methods.problem: CVRP (static, centralized)
sota_methods.key_idea: A genetic algorithm with a split procedure, penalized infeasible solutions, population diversity management and an efficient SWAP* inter-route neighborhood inside local search.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: CVRPLIB instances (X set)
sota_methods.reported_results: The PyVRP paper's Table 1 uses BKS from CVRPLIB. It reports a mean gap to BKS of 0.11% for HGS-CVRP (gap of mean 0.16%), against 0.22% for PyVRP and 0.21% for HGS-2012.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Centralized, static, CVRP only. There is no time-window, prize-collecting or communication model.

sota_methods.name: PyVRP (HGS for VRPTW and variants)
sota_methods.problem: VRPTW, PCVRPTW (prize-collecting / team-orienteering-style optional clients), MDVRPTW, HFVRP, multi-trip, PDPTW
sota_methods.key_idea: A polished HGS with its core in C++ and customization from Python. It descends from the ORTEC HGS that won the 2021 DIMACS VRPTW track and the OptiML solver that placed 1st in the EURO-NeurIPS 2022 static track.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Homberger-Gehring 1000-customer VRPTW; CVRPLIB; the benchmarks page in the documentation
sota_methods.reported_results: On 1000-customer HG VRPTW the mean gap to BKS is 0.40% (gap of mean 0.46%), against 0.32% for HGS-DIMACS. The documentation reports roughly 0.16-0.45% gaps on PCVRPTW and 0.44-1.08% on MDVRPTW, averaged over 10 seeds.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Centralized. Dynamic use only works by re-solving (not native). No communication or robustness model. It is the obvious centralized reference any decentralized claim must be measured against.

sota_methods.name: SISR (Slack Induction by String Removals), plus the open-source SISR for TOP/TOPTW/CTOP
sota_methods.venue: Transportation Science 54(2):417-433; extension at CPAIOR 2026 (LNCS 16595; Pajersky, Sobotka, Rudova)
sota_methods.problem: CVRP, VRPTW, PDPTW, TOP, TOPTW, CTOP
sota_methods.key_idea: A ruin-and-recreate local search: remove spatially adjacent strings of customers, then reinsert them greedily with blinks, under simulated-annealing acceptance. It is simple and fast, and it maps naturally onto per-robot 'drop a string, re-auction it'.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Standard VRP and OP benchmark sets. In the NDS paper, generated VRPTW/PCVRP instances.
sota_methods.reported_results: The CPAIOR 2026 open-source version reports 49 new BKS for TOP and about 85% of BKS matched across OP variants, with up to 10x speedup on large VRP instances. The README wording ('previously unknown optimal') differs from the abstract ('best-known'). In the NDS paper, at equal single-core time on generated VRPTW, SISRs beats PyVRP-HGS by 1.87%, 2.98% and 3.49% at N=500, 1000 and 2000.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Centralized. Matches only about 85% of OP-variant BKS, so it is not the TOP leader.

sota_methods.name: HALNS (Hybrid Adaptive LNS with set-packing) for TOP
sota_methods.problem: Team Orienteering Problem (static)
sota_methods.key_idea: ALNS destroy/repair plus local search, with a set-packing MIP that recombines the route pool.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Chao et al. (1996) TOP set (387 instances); Dang et al. (2013b) large-scale set (333 instances)
sota_methods.reported_results: Finds 386 of the 387 small-scale BKS and all large-scale BKS, and proves 3 new optima (CIRRELT working paper abstract).
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Static TOP is essentially saturated, so beating it needs new BKS with little headroom. Centralized.

sota_methods.name: ML-CO pipeline (Team Kleopatra), dynamic VRPTW with dispatch waves
sota_methods.venue: Transportation Science 58(4):708-725 (Baty, Jungel, Klein, Parmentier, Schiffer)
sota_methods.problem: Dynamic VRPTW: which requests to dispatch in each 1-hour epoch
sota_methods.key_idea: A GNN or linear model scores requests and feeds a prize-collecting HGS layer (a combinatorial-optimization layer). It is trained by imitating anticipative (hindsight) solutions with a Fenchel-Young loss.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: EURO Meets NeurIPS 2022 VRP competition (dynamic track)
sota_methods.reported_results: 1st on the dynamic track, final score 348,831.56 against 358,161.36 (Team SB) and 359,270.09 (OptiML). In the paper it is 5.15% above the anticipative baseline; greedy is 20.99% worse and Monte-Carlo sampling is 6.97% worse. It beats greedy by 13.18% and Monte-Carlo by 1.57%.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: A central dispatcher with one depot and no inter-vehicle communication model. The anticipative baseline is itself a heuristic HGS solution, not a bound.

sota_methods.name: OptiML: HGS plus scenario simulation (EURO-NeurIPS 2022)
sota_methods.venue: NeurIPS 2022 Competition Track, PMLR 220 (competition report by Kool et al.); team paper by van Doorn, Lan, Pentinga, Wouda
sota_methods.problem: Static and dynamic VRPTW
sota_methods.key_idea: A simplified, tuned HGS. For the dynamic variant it simulates future request scenarios and uses the static solver as an oracle to decide what to postpone.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: EURO-NeurIPS 2022 final set (100 hidden instances)
sota_methods.reported_results: Static 1st (157,188.67), dynamic 3rd (359,270.09), 2nd overall. The code became PyVRP.
sota_methods.code_url: https://github.com/ortec/euro-neurips-vrp-2022-quickstart (papers/OptiML.pdf; team code linked from the competition site)
sota_methods.license: Quickstart code MIT; instances CC BY-NC 4.0
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Centralized. Scenario sampling is costly.

sota_methods.name: Multiple Plan Approach (MPAc / MPAd) for the Dynamic Team Orienteering Problem
sota_methods.venue: European Journal of Operational Research 324(1):22-39 (Kirac, Milburn, Gedik)
sota_methods.problem: DTOP: some customers are revealed online, and 2-4 vehicles maximize collected profit within a time budget
sota_methods.key_idea: Keeps a pool of alternative routing plans and chooses actions online with two scoring functions (consensus-like 'c' and 'd'). It is compared with a CP-based offline optimum and a greedy policy.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: DTOP benchmark: 1161 instances built from the Chao TOP sets, at weak/moderate/high dynamism
sota_methods.reported_results: From the public results workbook (DTOP_Results_Tables.xlsx), counted over 1161 instances, #best is MPAd 969, MPAc 1041 and Greedy 619. Average deviation from the offline optimum (MPAd/MPAc/Greedy) is 17.6/17.4/23.6% for weak, 35.0/35.3/38.5% for moderate and 42.7/42.2/43.7% for high dynamism. Mean CPU time is about 175-207 s per instance, and about 700-760 s on set p7.
sota_methods.code_url: not found (unverified). Instances and per-instance results are public on Mendeley.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Centralized and slow. Under high dynamism it barely beats greedy (about 1 point), which points to an information-limited gap. No communication model.

sota_methods.name: Scen-RH-ALNS (scenario-sampling rolling-horizon ALNS) for DTOP-SC
sota_methods.venue: arXiv preprint (Wu, Shen, Zhou, Lei; Sichuan University)
sota_methods.problem: Dynamic TOP with time windows in spatial crowdsourcing; the DTOP benchmark as a special case
sota_methods.key_idea: At each epoch, add sampled virtual future tasks and solve the resulting deterministic TOPTW with ALNS (lookahead by scenario augmentation).
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Kirac et al. DTOP benchmark (1161 instances) plus synthetic map-based DTOP-SC instances
sota_methods.reported_results: High-dynamism mean profit 74.33, against MPAd 74.92 and MPAc 76.81 (0.8% and 3.2% lower). Takes 0.14 s per instance against about 192-198 s reported for MPA. In a three-way comparison it is best or tied on 708 of 1161 instances (MPAc 890, MPAd 975). It sets new best online results on 27/58/30 instances (high/moderate/weak). Mean gap to offline CP on high dynamism is 51.45%, against 51.24% (MPAd) and 50.48% (MPAc).
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Loses on average to MPA. Single-sample lookahead. Centralized. Not peer-reviewed.

sota_methods.name: Neural Deconstruction Search (NDS)
sota_methods.problem: CVRP, VRPTW, PCVRP
sota_methods.key_idea: A neural policy picks which customers to remove, greedy insertion rebuilds the solution, and batched GPU rollouts drive a simulated-annealing-style search.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Generated instances (N=100-2000); CVRP test sets from earlier NCO papers
sota_methods.reported_results: Against HGS or PyVRP-HGS at equal wall-clock time: CVRP N=2000 -2.34%, VRPTW N=2000 -3.50%, PCVRP N=2000 -4.60%. HGS still wins CVRP N=100. SISRs lands within about 0.01-0.3% of NDS on large instances.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Hardware asymmetry: an A100 GPU against 1-CPU-core baselines. Generated instances rather than BKS sets. Its margin over SISRs is tiny. Centralized.

sota_methods.name: Learning-guided Iterated Local Search for min-max mTSP
sota_methods.problem: Min-max multiple TSP (team makespan)
sota_methods.key_idea: Aggressive local search with probabilistic acceptance, and a multi-armed bandit that selects removal/insertion operators.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: 77 commonly used min-max mTSP benchmark instances
sota_methods.reported_results: 32 new best-known results; 35 others matched.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Centralized and single-depot. The prior SOTA is the memetic algorithm of He & Hao (EJOR 307:1055-1070, 2023). RL-CMSA (arXiv 2602.23579, 2026) claims to beat a hybrid GA on larger m.

sota_methods.name: PARCO (Parallel AutoRegressive Combinatorial Optimization)
sota_methods.problem: Multi-agent routing and scheduling (HCVRP, OMDCPDP, FFSP)
sota_methods.key_idea: All agents decode in parallel with transformer communication layers, multiple pointers and learned-priority conflict handlers.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Generated instances
sota_methods.reported_results: 3.3x-24.7x faster than sequential autoregressive baselines. Beats OR-Tools on large OMDCPDP.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Compared with OR-Tools and learned baselines, not with HGS/PyVRP or BKS. Centralized inference.

sota_methods.name: Equity-Transformer (min-max routing)
sota_methods.problem: Min-max mTSP and min-max mPDP
sota_methods.key_idea: Treats multi-agent min-max routing as sequential generation, with equity-context inductive biases.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Generated instances
sota_methods.reported_results: On mTSP with N=1000 and M=100: about 335x faster and about 53% lower cost than LKH3 (abstract).
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: The baseline is LKH3, not the min-max mTSP SOTA (He & Hao MA or ILS). No BKS instances. A typical neural-CO evaluation gap.

sota_methods.name: CBBA (baseline) and GACA (Grouping Auction-Consensus)
sota_methods.venue: CBBA: IEEE T-RO 25(4):912-926 (Choi, Brunet, How). GACA: arXiv 2026 (Rodriguez, Koenig, Dong, Lu)
sota_methods.problem: Decentralized multi-task multi-robot allocation, min-sum
sota_methods.key_idea: GACA replaces CBBA's single-task bids with group-level bids over nearest-neighbour task groups, resolved by consensus.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: 4,000 test worlds plus 3,280 instances (5-20 agents, 10-50 tasks) against a MILP optimum
sota_methods.reported_results: GACA reaches about 97% median optimality against 81-84% for CBBA.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Tiny instances, a custom testbed and no communication degradation. It shows how far CBBA is from optimal (16-19%).

sota_methods.name: LNS-Auction (decentralized LNS via combinatorial auctions)
sota_methods.problem: Heterogeneous multi-robot task allocation and sequencing (multi-vehicle GTSP, Dubins/DD robots)
sota_methods.key_idea: Each robot removes tasks from its own path (LNS destroy). The removed tasks are re-allocated by decentralized combinatorial auctions (repair) over a random communication graph.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Random instances and TSPLIB-derived instances against a centralized GTSP solver
sota_methods.reported_results: Deviation from the centralized solver averages 16% (max 37%), against 65% (max 76%) for CBBA-GLKH on random Dubins instances.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Closest prior art to 'CBBA plus LNS repair'. Still 16% from centralized. Evaluated with p=1.0 communication in the main tables and not against OR BKS.

sota_methods.name: Dec-MCTS
sota_methods.problem: Decentralized multi-robot planning (generalized team orienteering, active perception)
sota_methods.key_idea: Each robot runs MCTS and periodically exchanges compressed search-tree distributions, which are updated by variational-style distributed optimization. It is anytime and tolerates intermittent communication.
sota_methods.benchmark_used: Generalized team orienteering and active object recognition (custom)
sota_methods.reported_results: The abstract says it 'compares favorably to centralized MCTS even with severely degraded communication' (no BKS comparison).
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Measured only against centralized MCTS, not OR solvers or BKS.

sota_methods.name: CV-MRTA degraded-communication benchmark leaders (HIPC, DGA, DMCHBA)
sota_methods.problem: Decentralized collaborative-visit MRTA under packet loss
sota_methods.key_idea: Six non-learning decentralized allocators (CBAA, ACBBA, PI, HIPC, DMCHBA, DGA) are paired-compared across 25 communication conditions (Bernoulli, Gilbert-Elliott, Rayleigh).
sota_methods.benchmark_used: CV-MRTA (10-target grid scenarios)
sota_methods.reported_results: Mean MinSum under impaired communication: HIPC 66.95 steps, DGA 67.22. MinMax: DGA 24.49, DMCHBA 24.78. DMCHBA takes 4.88 ms and DGA 1.346 s.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Tiny instances (10 targets), no centralized optimum, not peer-reviewed.

sota_methods.name: PyVRP+ (LLM-driven metacognitive heuristic evolution for HGS)
sota_methods.problem: VRP variants on top of HGS/PyVRP
sota_methods.key_idea: An LLM runs a Reason-Act-Reflect loop to evolve HGS heuristics.
sota_methods.reported_results: Abstract claims up to 2.70% quality gain over the HGS baseline and more than 45% runtime reduction. Benchmark and time limits not checked beyond the abstract.
sota_methods.weaknesses_or_gaps: Improvement is over a PyVRP baseline at fixed budgets, not new BKS. It shows AAMAS accepts OR-grade routing work.

benchmarks.name: EURO Meets NeurIPS 2022 Vehicle Routing Competition (static and dynamic VRPTW)
benchmarks.problem_class: Static VRPTW, and dynamic VRPTW with stochastic request arrivals over 5-9 one-hour epochs with must-go requests. Real ORTEC grocery data, 200-900 customers.
benchmarks.metrics: Total driving time, lower is better, averaged over instances. The final phase allows 5-15 min for static and 2 min per epoch for dynamic.
benchmarks.baselines_included: HGS-VRPTW static solver; greedy, lazy and random dispatch; hindsight oracle; supervised and DQN ML baselines
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Yes. The final 100-instance table is in PMLR v220 (e.g., dynamic: Kleopatra 348,831.56, Team SB 358,161.36, OptiML 359,270.09), and a notebook reproducing it plus the finalists' solutions were published.
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: High. A NeurIPS competition with strong OR and ML teams, public environment and hidden-set numbers. Static is near-saturated (the organizers say so). Dynamic still has headroom: the best policy is 5.15% above the anticipative baseline.
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: High. Python gym-style environment, HGS C++ included, 250 public instances.

benchmarks.name: Dynamic Team Orienteering Problem (DTOP) benchmark (Kirac, Milburn, Gedik 2025)
benchmarks.problem_class: Online team orienteering. 2-4 vehicles, 30-100 requests (sets p1-p7 from Chao TOP), three degrees of dynamism, maximize collected profit within a time budget.
benchmarks.metrics: Total profit; deviation from the CP offline optimum; #instances best; CPU time
benchmarks.baselines_included: Per-instance values for the offline CP optimum (ZCP), MPAd, MPAc and Greedy, with CPU times, in DTOP_Results_Tables.xlsx
benchmarks.has_leaderboard_or_published_numbers: Yes, per instance (1161 instances) in the dataset workbook, plus the Scen-RH-ALNS (2026) aggregates
benchmarks.code_url: none found; 1168 txt instance and degree-of-dynamism files plus the xlsx
benchmarks.credibility_for_sota_claim: Medium. EJOR 2025 with objective per-instance numbers, but it is new, has only about 2 methods reported, and under high dynamism greedy sits within about 1 point of MPA (information-limited). Weak and moderate dynamism leave about 6 and 3 points of algorithmic room between greedy and MPA, and 17-35% to offline.
benchmarks.ease_of_adoption: High. Small text instances, public baselines, and runs on CPU in seconds.

benchmarks.name: Chao et al. (1996) TOP set plus Dang et al. (2013) large-scale TOP
benchmarks.problem_class: Static team orienteering (profit maximization with a time budget per vehicle)
benchmarks.metrics: Total profit against BKS or proven optimum; CPU time

open_gaps: No accepted benchmark jointly scores OR-grade solution quality (gap to BKS or optimum) and robustness to communication loss. OR BKS sets (Chao TOP, TOPTW, HG VRPTW, CVRPLIB) assume one central solver. Decentralized MRTA evaluations use tiny custom instances: CV-MRTA (2026) has 10 targets and no centralized optimum, and GACA (2026) uses at most 50 tasks against a MILP.

This sweep found no 2023-2026 paper claiming that a CBBA-like or consensus decentralized algorithm with LNS repair comes within about 1% of centralized BKS on a standard OR instance set. The closest are Sadeghi & Smith 2017 (LNS-Auction, 16% average deviation from a centralized GTSP solver), Kalina 2014 thesis (agent-based VRPTW with 0.3% relative error in vehicle count, not distance, with simulated agents and no communication limits), Dec-MCTS 2019 (only against centralized MCTS) and consensus-ADMM 2025 (arXiv 2511.12879, 'near-centralized', no routing BKS). The search budget ran out before exhaustive coverage.

CBBA-family quality is measurably poor: 81-84% of the MILP optimum (GACA 2026) and 65% average excess over a centralized GTSP solver (CBBA-GLKH in Sadeghi & Smith). Bundle-level local search or LNS is an under-exploited lever. The bundle-length tradeoff alone shifts cost by 14-42% under packet loss (arXiv 2609.06273).

Static TOP and HG VRPTW are saturated: HALNS matches 386/387 and all large-scale TOP BKS, and PyVRP is within 0.40% on HG1000. A 'SOTA' claim there needs new BKS and heavy compute, and decentralization does not help.

Dynamic benchmarks with public numbers (EURO-NeurIPS dynamic, DTOP) are single-dispatcher and centralized, with no communication or partial-information model across vehicles. Under high DTOP dynamism greedy is within about 1 point of MPA (43.7% against 42.2-42.7% deviation from offline), so much of the roughly 50% gap to offline is the value of perfect information, not algorithm quality.

Neural multi-agent CO papers (Equity-Transformer, PARCO, DPN, NDS) mostly compare with LKH3, OR-Tools or single-core HGS on generated instances, often with GPU-versus-1-CPU asymmetry. OR reviewers discount these claims, so a fair-hardware, BKS-anchored comparison is missing.

EURO-NeurIPS dynamic: the best published policy (ML-CO) is still 5.15% above the anticipative HGS baseline, and that baseline is not a lower bound. The only follow-up found (Learning with Local Search MCMC Layers, arXiv 2505.14240) reports no leaderboard-comparable numbers on the competition page.

The researcher's own prior result (local fallback matters more than clever query selection) implies any new decentralized SOTA claim must beat a strong 'central PyVRP re-solve plus local fallback' baseline under the same loss model. No published paper runs that comparison.

sota_opportunities.idea: Consensus-LNS for dynamic team orienteering. Each robot keeps a CBBA bundle and improves it with SISR string-removal repair, re-auctioning removed strings through consensus messages, with lightweight scenario sampling for lookahead (Scen-RH-style virtual tasks). Anytime, so it degrades gracefully under Bernoulli or Gilbert-Elliott loss. Report two results: (a) centralized-equivalent performance (perfect links) against the published per-instance MPAc/MPAd/Greedy/offline-CP values; (b) a new axis of profit retained under loss, against a central-dispatcher-plus-fallback baseline.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: DTOP benchmark (Kirac et al. 2025, 1161 instances, CC BY 4.0), with TOPTW Solomon/Cordeau instances as a static sanity anchor
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: DTOP is new (EJOR 2025) and has only two published methods: MPA, which is slow (about 175-207 s average, about 700+ s on p7), and Scen-RH-ALNS, which loses to MPA on average. Nobody has run it decentralized or with communication loss. Per-instance published numbers make a new-best-online-result claim objective. Weak and moderate dynamism leave 17-35% to offline and about 3-6 points between greedy and MPA.
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: MPAc: #best 1041/1161, deviation from offline 17.4/35.3/42.2% (weak/moderate/high). MPAd: 969/1161, 17.6/35.0/42.7%. Greedy: 619/1161. Scen-RH-ALNS: high-dynamism mean profit 74.33 at 0.14 s. Plus a PyVRP prize-collecting re-solve baseline (with optional clients) and CBBA/ACBBA/PI/HIPC run in the same simulator.
sota_opportunities.risk: Under high dynamism the headroom is information-limited, so expect 1-3% gains. The benchmark is niche, and reviewers may ask why not EURO-NeurIPS. The decentralized variant has no prior numbers, so comparisons under loss rest on your own simulator (the old self-built-testbed criticism). Mitigate with the exact published instances, a pre-registered loss model and a strong centralized-plus-fallback baseline.

sota_opportunities.idea: Decentralized anytime population search. Robots gossip elite routes (HGS/SISR fragments) and resolve conflicts by consensus (CBBA winner tables). Publish the curve of gap to BKS against packet-loss rate and robot count on standard static instances, showing near-BKS quality with ideal links and the smallest degradation under loss. Evaluate the same algorithm on CV-MRTA against its six decentralized allocators.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: TOPTW (Solomon/Cordeau), HG VRPTW 200-400-customer subsets, the Chao TOP set, and the CV-MRTA degraded-communication benchmark
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: The OR and decentralized MRTA communities do not overlap. OR reports gap to BKS with a central solver; MRTA reports relative performance of CBBA variants on 10-50-task toys. LNS-Auction (2017) showed decentralized LNS can close CBBA's 65% gap to about 16%, but nobody has pushed this to BKS-grade gaps with modern HGS/SISR operators or measured it against loss.
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: Centralized PyVRP (0.40% gap on HG1000), HALNS (TOP BKS), open-source SISR (TOPTW), and for decentralized methods HIPC (MinSum 66.95 under impairment) and DGA/DMCHBA (MinMax 24.49/24.78) on CV-MRTA. Also LNS-Auction (16% from centralized) and CBBA (81-84% of optimum).
sota_opportunities.risk: With perfect links a decentralized method will not beat PyVRP or HALNS, so the SOTA claim must be framed as 'best under loss' or 'Pareto-optimal in quality versus communication'. That framing is weaker than a plain SOTA. CV-MRTA has no license (run locally, do not redistribute). Reviewers may prefer 'central solver plus periodic broadcast' as the natural baseline, and the method must beat it.

sota_opportunities.idea: Dynamic dispatch with GPU-trained learned dispatch plus a consensus-of-scenarios dispatcher on PyVRP. Combine Baty-style imitation of anticipative solutions (GNN on 4xH100) with a Bent & Van Hentenryck MSA consensus function over many sampled scenarios, solved in parallel on 96 cores. Goal: beat ML-CO on the published final instance set under the competition time limits.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: EURO Meets NeurIPS 2022 dynamic VRPTW (final 100-instance protocol, reproducible notebook)
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: ML-CO is still 5.15% above the anticipative baseline, and Monte-Carlo sampling was only 1.57% behind ML-CO with limited scenarios. Large-scale parallel scenario solving and better imitation targets are unexplored (the authors note the anticipative target may not be the best one to imitate).
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: Kleopatra/ML-CO 348,831.56 (final dynamic score), Team SB 358,161.36, OptiML 359,270.09; greedy baseline (20.99% worse than anticipative in Baty et al.)
sota_opportunities.risk: High-quality incumbents leave small margins (1-3%). Hardware normalization against 2022 time limits is contestable, since 96 cores for scenarios is not the competition setup. It is a centralized problem, so the CBBA and multi-robot framing does not fit. The instances are non-commercial.

sota_opportunities.idea: LLM-evolved bid and repair operators for decentralized allocation. Use the PyVRP+/VRPAgent style of LLM heuristic discovery to evolve CBBA scoring functions and LNS repair operators inside a communication-loss simulator. Train on held-out DTOP, TOPTW and CV-MRTA splits, then evaluate on untouched splits.
sota_opportunities.target_benchmark: DTOP (held-out problem sets), TOPTW, CV-MRTA
sota_opportunities.why_gap_exists: LLM-driven heuristic discovery has reached AAMAS 2026 (PyVRP+) and drove CVRPLib XL BKS improvements, but it has only targeted centralized solvers. Decentralized bid and repair rules are hand-designed and known to be far from optimal.
sota_opportunities.baselines_to_beat: Hand-designed CBBA/ACBBA/PI/HIPC, MPA (DTOP), and the SISR repair operator
sota_opportunities.risk: Novelty may be judged incremental over PyVRP+ and VRPAgent. Evolved operators overfit to the simulator. Compute and API costs are high. Needs strict held-out splits to avoid benchmark leakage.

missing_items.item: LoRR 2026 official results and setup (missing from every sweep; the sweeps called them unverified or pending). Results were announced on 2 Sep 2026. Task Scheduling track: 1st Team No Man's Sky, 2nd Trzy Kwaterki, 3rd hcp. Combined track: 1st No Man's Sky. Execution track: 1st mygo. SmartPath had placed 1st in Scheduling before it and team wonder were disqualified for code transfer and account sharing. The round had 69 teams and 3,361 submissions. The 2026 'uncertainty' is stochastic per-tick execution delays, which the CFP describes as 'mechanical issues or communication delays'. It is not message loss, so LoRR still does not test degraded-communication allocation. The 2026 instances and code are not archived yet: Benchmark-Archive was last pushed 2025-05-09, and the organizers say codes and solutions 'will be archived'. The 2026 Expo tech reports are due 9 Oct 2026 and the event is 3 Nov 2026, so the 2026 methods will become public soon.
missing_items.why_it_matters: This is the only AAMAS-co-hosted leaderboard for group task scheduling. The 2024 scheduling SOTA (No Man's Sky) is also the 2026 scheduling SOTA, so any LoRR SOTA claim has to beat that team's archived code. The winners' write-ups will appear within weeks, which could raise the bar mid-project.

missing_items.item: Ideal-communication and static pre-allocation numbers for CV_MRTA. The sweeps compared impaired means only against a lower bound. Async, ideal links: DGA MinMax 21.93 and HIPC MinSum 52.62. Impaired means: 24.49 and 66.95. Paper Table (ideal pre-allocation medians): DGA MinMax 21.0 and MinSum 50.0, HIPC MinSum 51.5, DMCHBA 22.5 / 70.0. The recomputed collision-free lower bound on the 500 core instances has median 20 / 50 and mean 19.65 / 49.33.
missing_items.why_it_matters: With ideal links, the best existing planners are already within about 0-5% of the bound at the median. The large gap (about 12% on MinMax, about 27% on MinSum) is the drop from ideal to impaired links, caused by online reallocation under loss. The target is therefore 'hold ideal-link quality under loss', not '1.05x optimum'. This changes both the size and the novelty of any claim on that benchmark.

missing_items.item: Collision-aware exact references on grids: target-assignment-and-path-finding (TAPF) and multi-goal TAPF. CBS-TA (Hönig et al., AAMAS 2018; code in libMultiRobotPlanning, MIT). ITA-CBS (Tang, Ren, Li, Sycara 2023; code ITA-CBS2, GPL-3.0). MG-TAPF, the optimal and bounded-suboptimal multi-goal version (Zhong, Li, Koenig, Ma, ICRA 2022).
missing_items.why_it_matters: CV_MRTA-style instances (4 robots, 10 goals, 4-connected grid) are exactly MG-TAPF. These solvers can turn the Manhattan lower bound used in sweep 5 into a collision-aware optimum or bounded reference. They are also an established AAMAS/ICRA coordination arena that the sweeps omit entirely.

missing_items.item: Decentralized and delay-robust MAPD baselines: Token Passing (Ma, Li, Kumar, Koenig, AAMAS 2017); k-TP and p-TP robust MAPD with delays (Lodigiani, Basilico, Amigoni 2023); RMCA integrated assignment and path planning for capacitated MAPD (Chen et al., RA-L 2021); online MAPD with task deadlines (IROS 2024).
missing_items.why_it_matters: These are the decentralized and robust baselines reviewers will expect for any lifelong or group-mission claim under delays, which is the LoRR 2026 regime. Token Passing is the canonical decentralized MAPD method, and a CBBA-derived scheduler needs to be positioned against it.

missing_items.item: CFSTP / D-CTS: coalition formation with spatial and temporal constraints (Capezzuto, Tarapore, Ramchurn; EUMAS 2021 and SN Computer Science 2021). It is a distributed, dynamic allocation benchmark built from public London Fire Brigade records: 347,588 tasks, up to 150 agents and 3,000 tasks. D-CTS completes 3.79% more tasks than DSA-SDP (a DCOP method). Java code, MIT.
missing_items.why_it_matters: It is the AAMAS community's own real-data benchmark for decentralized, deadline-driven, coalition allocation, and it has few follow-ups, so it is winnable. None of the sweeps mention it, yet it matches 'group missions with deadlines' better than CV_MRTA does.

missing_items.item: DCOP / max-sum decentralized coordination (Ramchurn, Farinelli, Macarthur, Jennings, 'Decentralized Coordination in RoboCup Rescue', The Computer Journal 2010) and DSA-style DCOP baselines.
missing_items.why_it_matters: AAMAS area chairs will ask why DCOP (max-sum or DSA) baselines are missing from a decentralized-allocation SOTA claim. The sweeps only mention a RoboCup Rescue DCOP module in passing.

missing_items.item: Distributed submodular coordination under limited communication, which gives guarantee-bearing alternatives to CBBA's 50% bound: resource-aware distributed submodular maximization (Xu & Tzoumas, CDC 2022); bandit submodular coordination (RSS 2023); MA-OSMA/MA-OSEA with a (1-e^-c)/c guarantee over non-complete graphs (Zhang et al., ICLR 2025); SubMAPG, CTDE policy gradient with a stagewise 1/2 guarantee (arXiv 2605.13269).
missing_items.why_it_matters: Sweep 1 proposes 'guarantee-preserving learned bidding'. Reviewers at RSS, CDC or T-RO will cite this line as prior art and as baselines, and SubMAPG is already learned plus a 1/2 guarantee plus decentralized execution.

missing_items.item: DynaHMRC (arXiv 2606.14882, June 2026): decentralized heterogeneous multi-robot collaboration in which each robot is an LLM agent. Allocation happens through leadership bidding and leader election, with fine-tuned domain LLMs and its own dynamic-task benchmark.
missing_items.why_it_matters: It is the closest recent prior art for any 'language-model agent plus bidding' hybrid in the CBJA/System-1 lineage. Sweep 4 cites it only for its context-bottleneck remark.

missing_items.item: The newest CBBA variant: CBBA combined with Graphs of Convex Sets for task allocation and motion planning with dynamic tasks in cluttered environments (arXiv 2606.18516, AIAA SciTech 2027 submission).
missing_items.why_it_matters: It completes the 2026 CBBA-family map (alongside GACA, learned-bid CBBA, ED-CBBA and CC-OPI). It shows the trend is coupling allocation with trajectory feasibility, and that is a novelty check for any CBBA-derived claim.

missing_items.item: DTOP instance-level structure (computed here from the public results workbook). 50.2% of the 1,161 instances are three-way ties between MPAd, MPAc and Greedy, and 11.6% have offline optimum 0. Under high dynamism 76.7% are ties. The Summary sheet confirms #best counts of 969 (MPAd), 1,041 (MPAc) and 619 (Greedy). suspicious_claims.claim: Sweep 5: CV_MRTA is 'near-degenerate'. The best methods sit 24.6% (MinMax) and 35.7% (MinSum) above optimum, and a replicated planner would reach at most 1.05x optimum in every condition with no allocation messages, a 15-40% margin.
suspicious_claims.verdict: PARTLY RIGHT, OVERSTATED. The arithmetic and the degeneracy intuition hold. The 'optimum' is a collision-free, turn-free Manhattan lower bound, not an achievable optimum. Most of the gap comes from reallocation under loss, not from planning. The replicated-planner idea is essentially DMCHBA with a better solver.
suspicious_claims.evidence: I re-ran opt.py/opt.csv: Held-Karp plus subset DP on Manhattan distance with starts (0,0),(0,6),(0,12),(0,18), giving means 19.65/49.33 and medians 20/50. The paper states realized steps include intent-layer collision-safe detours, heading-change cost and duplicate visits. Ideal-link async best values are DGA 21.93 and HIPC 52.62, i.e. 11.6% and 6.7% above the bound even with perfect communication. Ideal pre-allocation medians are DGA 21.0/50.0 and HIPC 51.5, essentially at the bound. DMCHBA already plans with 0 messages in pre-allocation (communication_attempted_median=0, first feasible in round 1). The realistic target is ideal-link quality under loss: roughly 10-12% on MinMax and 20-27% on MinSum over impaired means. Reviewers will call 'never reallocate on a static, fully known instance' a benchmark artifact.

shortlist_arenas.arena: 1. LoRR Task-Scheduling track (planner and executor fixed): a market or consensus scheduler with GPU-trained regional guidance. Highest reviewer credibility.
shortlist_arenas.benchmark: League of Robot Runners: the 2024 main-round instances with best-known solutions (Benchmark-Archive, 10 instances up to 10k agents) via Start-Kit v3.1.0 (MIT). Add the 2026 stochastic-delay instances once archived.
shortlist_arenas.metric: Tasks finished per instance and the normalized track score (sum of ratio to best-known), within the official per-step compute limits.
shortlist_arenas.strongest_baseline_with_code: Team No Man's Sky scheduler (2024 Scheduler 6.876, e.g. WAREHOUSE 146,398 and SORTATION 146,375 tasks; also 2026 Scheduling winner). Code is in the Code-Archive, which has no license, so run it unmodified. Also Team_verstand (6.375) and the default greedy. GRAND (arXiv 2512.03194) has no code and reports +10% over the 2024 winner on at most 500-agent maps.
shortlist_arenas.why_winnable: GRAND shows learned guidance plus min-cost-flow plus local assignment beats the heuristic winner by about 10% at 200-500 agents. Nobody has published on the official 10k-agent instances. The scheduler track isolates allocation, 4xH100 covers GNN guidance training and 96 cores cover parallel evaluation. The venue is AAMAS-co-hosted, so an externally anchored win reads as SOTA.
shortlist_arenas.risks: Heavy C++ engineering at 10k agents within 1 s. The work is centralized, so the degraded-communication identity is lost (2026 models execution delays only). The 2026 instances and code are not archived yet, and the 2026 winners' reports (due 9 Oct 2026) may raise the bar. Gains on huge maps may be planner-limited. The Code-Archive has no license.

shortlist_arenas.arena: 2. Decentralized MRTA under degraded communication: a loss-robust commitment and re-auction protocol. Best fit to the CBBA lineage and highest winnability, but low credibility unless extended.
shortlist_arenas.benchmark: CV_MRTA_Benchmark (Lott & Honary, arXiv 2609.13711): 500 paired instances x 25 communication conditions plus its scale campaign. Add a Nayak-2020-style search-and-visit variant (unknown targets) and dynamic arrivals so information is actually private.
shortlist_arenas.metric: Realized MinMax and MinSum steps, mean over the 24 impaired conditions (paired), plus publications per team step and compute. Report the ratio to the ideal-link best (21.93 / 52.62) and to a collision-aware reference (MG-TAPF/CBS-TA), not only the Manhattan bound (19.65 / 49.33).
shortlist_arenas.strongest_baseline_with_code: DGA (MinMax 24.49 impaired, 21.93 ideal), DMCHBA (24.78; 2.08 publications per step; 4.88 ms) and HIPC (MinSum 66.95 impaired, 52.62 ideal), all in https://github.com/jlott22/CV_MRTA_Benchmark (no license; written permission needed).
shortlist_arenas.why_winnable: The ideal-to-impaired drop (about 2.6 MinMax steps, about 12%, and about 14 MinSum steps, about 27%) comes from online reallocation under loss, not planning quality, and existing planners are near the bound under ideal links. A CBBA-derived hybrid that commits to a replicated a-priori plan and re-auctions only on confirmed deviations, with loss-adaptive depth, should hold near-ideal quality in every condition. That margin is far above noise with 500 paired instances.
shortlist_arenas.risks: Degeneracy: static, fully known instances let 'never reallocate' win, and DMCHBA is already replicated planning, so reviewers may call the win trivial. The claim must rest on the private-information and dynamic extension. The benchmark has no license, is a two-week-old preprint and is tiny (4 robots, 10 targets). Repeating the CBJA mistake of a self-built extension is a risk; mitigate by pre-registering and contributing the extension upstream.

shortlist_arenas.arena: 3. Online team orienteering: consensus-LNS with parallel scenario sampling. An OR-grade anchor with per-instance published baselines.
shortlist_arenas.benchmark: Dynamic Team Orienteering Problem (Kirac, Milburn, Gedik, EJOR 2025): 1,161 instances at weak, moderate and high dynamism. Data and per-instance results at https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/xnf6c4d5gt/1 (CC BY 4.0).
shortlist_arenas.metric: Collected profit per instance, percent of the offline CP optimum, and #instances best computed on non-tied instances, plus CPU time.
shortlist_arenas.strongest_baseline_with_code: No baseline code exists, but per-instance results are public, so no reimplementation is needed. MPAc has #best 1041/1161 at about 190-226 s mean CPU; MPAd 969; Greedy 619. Scen-RH-ALNS (arXiv 2601.11010, no code) is fast (0.14 s) but weaker than MPA on average.
shortlist_arenas.why_winnable: Under weak dynamism MPAc collects 35.2% of total profit against 39.6% offline and Greedy 28.7%, which leaves real algorithmic headroom. Moderate dynamism is 20.5% vs 29.0%. A CBBA-style bundle maintenance with SISR string-removal repair and scenario lookahead parallelized on 96 cores can target new best-online results at 10-100x lower runtime. The published numbers are objective and EJOR-anchored.
shortlist_arenas.risks: It is a niche benchmark. About 50% of instances are three-way ties and 11.6% are trivial, and under high dynamism the gap is information-limited. The setting is centralized, so a decentralized or lossy variant would have no prior numbers. Runtime comparison against the paper's hardware is contestable.

shortlist_arenas.arena: 4. Heterogeneous coalition MRTA at scale: learned scoring plus consensus coalition auction plus LNS repair.
shortlist_arenas.benchmark: HeteroMRTA RALTestSet (RA-L 2025) and the Sadcher MRTA-Benchmark 250K and scaling protocol (MRS 2025; 3, 5 or 20 robots; up to 250 tasks). Data: https://data.4tu.nl/datasets/10e28ee0-9ad9-450d-8be7-6e6a91f2931f (CC BY 4.0).
shortlist_arenas.metric: Makespan. Percent gap to MILP where MILP solves (8 tasks x 3 robots), and makespan against Greedy and the learned methods at large scale.
shortlist_arenas.strongest_baseline_with_code: S-Sadcher (3.8% gap; https://github.com/jakbichler/Sadcher, no license), HeteroMRTA (https://github.com/marmotlab/HeteroMRTA, Apache-2.0), CTAS-D Gurobi MILP, and Greedy, which beats S-Sadcher at 20 robots once tasks exceed about 70.
shortlist_arenas.why_winnable: Both learned methods fall apart exactly where teams are large (20 robots, more than 70 tasks) and greedy wins. A hybrid that uses an H100-trained scorer only to weight a CBBA/CBGA-style coalition auction and then repairs with CPU LNS can keep greedy's robustness while adding learned lookahead. A clear margin over greedy and S-Sadcher at scale is plausible within 6-10 weeks.
shortlist_arenas.risks: The setting is centralized with ideal communication. The benchmark comes from a single lab with modest venue tier. There is no ground-truth optimum at scale. The small-scale MILP gap (3.8%) is tight, and the Sadcher code has no license.

shortlist_arenas.arena: 5. MILP-referenced decentralized mTSP/MRTA under lossy links: guarantee-aware grouped-bid CBBA with post-consensus local search.
shortlist_arenas.benchmark: The GACA protocol (arXiv 2608.15884) reimplemented: 5-20 agents, 10-50 tasks, MILP ground truth. Add Bernoulli, Gilbert-Elliott and Rayleigh loss following CV_MRTA's channel models, and use the GCBBA public code (ECAI 2025).
shortlist_arenas.metric: Median percent of MILP optimum as a function of loss rate, plus convergence rounds and messages.
shortlist_arenas.strongest_baseline_with_code: GCBBA and CBBA via https://github.com/Khaalex1/Global_Consensus_Based_Bundle_Algorithm (no license file). CBBA reaches 81-84% of optimum. GACA reaches about 97% with ideal links but has no code. Learned-bid CBBA (arXiv 2605.21932) has no code.
shortlist_arenas.why_winnable: No published method reports percent of optimum under loss. CBBA-family consensus degrades with loss, while GACA is ideal-link only. Holding at least 95% median optimality at 30-50% loss would be a clear, MILP-anchored margin.
shortlist_arenas.risks: The instance generator is self-built (weaker than an external leaderboard, and the CBJA trap). A GACA reimplementation can be disputed. Under ideal links there are only about 3 points of headroom. The Koenig/Rodriguez group is actively publishing in this exact direction, so the scoop risk is high.
